description: Blodomloppet in Uppsala is a fun run that raises awareness of the vital importance of blood donation and welcomes participants to walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km. The event also offers Specialomloppet and Lilla Blodomloppet for younger participants. The courses are partly officially measured, and the event ends with a shared picnic, creating a social and inclusive atmosphere. Blodomloppet is a health and wellness activity that brings together individuals and teams, with a strong focus on health and the importance of blood donation.
course_highlights: The 10 km course is officially measured
The 5 km course is approximately 4,950 metres long
Lilla Blodomloppet is 2.5 km long
additional: Team registration is for 5 people. Large registrations can be made using an Excel template. The 10 km course is officially measured; the other courses are approximate. The event ends with a shared picnic. Water stations and medical services are available on site. Race bibs, changing facilities and toilets are available. Participants may also take part with a dog. Environmental sustainability and accessibility are prioritised. The event is part of Sweden’s largest blood donation race and aims to promote blood donation while offering a social, healthy event for all ages.

name: Bėgimas „Kutaliai – Kaltinėnai“
description: The “Kutaliai–Kaltinėnai” Run is a traditional cross-country race held to commemorate the 141st anniversary of the birth of Aleksandras Stulginskis, President of the Republic of Lithuania, and Constituent Assembly Day. The competition takes place in hilly terrain, promoting physical activity and respect for sport. The start is in Kutaliai village, and the finish is at the stadium of Aleksandras Stulginskis Gymnasium in Kaltinėnai, Šilalė District. The event is intended for school athletes from cities and districts, as well as anyone else who meets the health requirements.
course_highlights: Start in Kutaliai village; finish at Kaltinėnai Gymnasium stadium
Cross-country race over hilly terrain
Held in memory of Aleksandras Stulginskis, President of the Republic of Lithuania
additional: Registration is open until 9:30 a.m. on race day at Aleksandras Stulginskis Gymnasium in Kaltinėnai. Participants must provide a doctor’s certificate or an entry form with a doctor’s approval. All participants receive commemorative medals, and the group winners receive medals for first, second, and third place. Athletes of various ages take part in the event; registration and health checks are required, and winners and participants are awarded.

name: Blodomloppet
organizer: Stora Tuna OK och Kvarnsvedens GOIF Friidrott
description: Blodomloppet in Borlänge is an inclusive recreational event where you can walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km, or take part in Lilla Blodomloppet (approximately 800 m). The event is organised locally by Stora Tuna OK and Kvarnsvedens GOIF Friidrott and has a strong social focus, with team registration and a picnic to round off the event. It aims to raise awareness of blood donation and welcomes both individual participants and teams. Information and practical details (race bibs, storage, start areas) are published on the event page.
course_highlights: The 5 km and 10 km running routes head north across Sportfältet and split at Storsvängen
The walking route heads down towards central Borlänge and finishes by the fruit and medal tables
Lilla Blodomloppet is approximately 800 m and takes place in the area around the event venue
additional: You can register individually or as a team (3–5 people; a picnic bag is included). Teams cannot register late after 21 May; individual participants can register late through the system until 28 May at 12:00. Late registration on race day is available at the event venue from 15:00 to 17:00 and payment is by Swish only (400 kr). Race bibs can be collected at Friskis&Svettis (Skomakargatan 9) on 24 May from 13:00 to 16:00. Blood donors receive a 40 kr discount per person. The kiosk at the event venue accepts Swish only. Team registration for 3–5 participants includes a picnic bag. Individual registration is also available; blood donors receive a 40 kr discount per person. The start is at 17:00, with a warm-up at 16:45 (according to the information provided). The routes include 5 km, 10 km and Lilla Blodomloppet, which is approximately 800 m; registration is via the website or in person at Sportfältet from around 15:00. The race package includes a technical T-shirt, race bib and medal.

name: Vårruset
description: Vårruset in Örebro is part of Sweden’s largest fitness tour for women and takes place on Thursday, 28 May 2026, at Gustavsviksbadet. Runners can choose between 2.5 km and a certified 5 km course. Both individual entries and team entries (teams of 5) are welcome. Participants receive a medal, a finish-line bag and a race bib, with optional timing. Teams that register are treated to a picnic after finishing. The event is organised locally by KFUM Örebro Friidrott in collaboration with Marathongruppen and other local clubs.
course_highlights: Choose between 2.5 km and a certified 5 km course
Evening race at Gustavsviksbadet, starting at 18:30
Picnic after the finish for teams of five
additional: Registration is online and open until race day, up to 1 hour before the first start. Individual entries include a medal, a finish-line bag and a race bib, plus timing for those who choose it. Timing can be declined so that results are not published. Recommended ages: 5 km from age 13 (age 11 when accompanied by an adult); 2.5 km from age 11 (age 7 when accompanied by an adult). There is also a digital option (Vårruset Digitalt), where the medal is sent after the tour ends and team registration is not available. Distances: 2.5 km or 5 km; team registration includes a picnic; age recommendations: 5 km, age 13 (age 11 when accompanied by an adult); 2.5 km, age 11 (age 7 when accompanied by an adult). Event area at Gustavsviksbadet; online registration and binding entry.

description: The 3rd Benno Viirand Memorial Fun Run is a family-friendly running and Nordic walking event held in the small town of Mustla. The race takes place on a 5 km course that starts near the Vambola bus stop in Soe village and finishes at the Tarvastu Gymnasium stadium. The event aims to honor the memory of legendary runner Benno Viirand and promote running as a healthy way to spend leisure time. In addition to the main race, free children’s races take place at the stadium. Participants are provided with race numbers and can register in advance or at the venue on race day.
course_highlights: 5 km course from the Vambola bus stop in Soe village to the Tarvastu Gymnasium stadium
Nordic walkers can also take part in the main distance
Children’s races take place at the stadium after the main race starts
additional: Bus transport to the start is provided from Tarvastu Gymnasium stadium at 17:50; if needed, the bus will make two trips. Race-day registration at the start venue is open from 17:30 to 18:15. Participation in the children’s races is free. Competitors can collect their race numbers before the start on race day. The participation fee must be paid to the bank account. Registration is open until 27.05.2026. Safety and responsibility are the participants’ own responsibility.

name: Eksjö Stadslopp
description: Welcome to Eksjö Stadslopp on Friday 29 May 2026—a Friday evening race in the beautiful wooden town of Eksjö. The race programme includes the classic 10 km, a 5 km fun run, and children’s and youth races (1000 m and 600 m). The finish is at Stora Torget, and proceeds from the event go to Eksjö Södra IK’s children’s and youth activities. The 10 km and 5 km courses are officially measured, and the event welcomes runners of all ages.
course_highlights: The race runs through Eksjö’s historic wooden town
Finish in the middle of Stora Torget in Eksjö
The 10 km and 5 km courses are officially measured
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Snäckan (next to the swimming pool). Collection times: Thursday 28 May, 17:00–20:00, and Friday 29 May from 14:00. Changing facilities are available at Prästängshallen until 21:30 on race day. Late registration opens on 24 May for an increased fee and is available until one hour before the start of each race category via the same registration page. All finishers in the 600 m and 1000 m races receive a medal; finishers in the 5 km and 10 km receive a plaque. There is a sprint prize on the 10 km course after approximately 1.2 km (for the first man and woman, who must finish the race). Categories are determined by year of birth. Group registration by invoice: tavling.esik@gmail.com. Course maps can be collected at Snäckan on Thursday and Friday. Late registration opens on 24 May for an increased fee; race bibs can be collected at Snäckan by the swimming pool; parking is available at Storegårdsgatan 3A, Eksjö; changing facilities are available at Prästängshallen until 21:30 on race day.

name: adidas Shake Out Run
description: Get a taste of the unique marathon atmosphere by running the adidas Shake Out Run. The race is 5 km long, with the start and finish at Stockholm Olympic Stadium. It’s the perfect warm-up for anyone running the marathon the next day, but also an opportunity for others to experience the atmosphere during event weekend. The first 1,000 people to register are guaranteed an adidas T-shirt in their chosen size.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Stockholm Olympic Stadium
5 km course—a short race that’s perfect as a warm-up
Take part for a taste of the marathon atmosphere during event weekend
additional: The race is organised by athletics clubs Hässelby SK and Spårvägens FK. Minimum age: 13 (11 when accompanied by a guardian). The first 1,000 people to register are guaranteed an adidas T-shirt, distributed at the race; others can check at the information desk after the race to see which sizes remain. Payment options: online banking, Visa/Mastercard, Swish or invoice via Klarna. Late registration is available online until 1 hour before the first start. Minimum age: 13; eco-friendly transport options to the event area (metro/bus or bicycle); registration is through a participant account; T-shirts and sizes are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis and collected at the information desk.

The race is part of the 2026 Maru Lake Runs series and is its second event. There are refreshment points along the course, which is marked and secured by course marshals. Nordic walkers and walkers are also welcome; they start in the last group. The event center is at the start-finish area, where race numbers are also distributed and the awards ceremony takes place.
course_highlights: A 6.5 km loop around Lake Harku
Refreshment points at the 3 km mark and at the finish
Course marshals and a marked route

The awards ceremony is scheduled for approximately 13:00, with awards for the top 6 men and women and the age-group winners. The event has two distances and children's races; registration opens at 9:30 and the start is at 12:00. Participants can enjoy nature and a healthy lifestyle.

name: Koeru kergejõustikuvõistlused
location: Koeru KK staadion, Koeru, Järva County, Estonia
description: The Koeru athletics competition is a traditional track and field event held at the Koeru KK stadium. Men and women compete in two age groups across several events, including the 100 m, long jump, shot put, discus throw, javelin throw and 1000 m. The winner is determined by adding the points from their three best events. The competition is open to everyone, who may take part in all events. Young athletes use throwing implements appropriate for their age group.
course_highlights: Events: 100 m, long jump, shot put, discus throw, javelin throw and 1000 m
There are 4 attempts in the long jump and throwing events
The competition takes place at Koeru KK stadium
additional: In the men’s and women’s competitions, the winner of the three-event competition is awarded a cup, and places 2–6 receive medals. Winners of individual events are awarded medals. Young athletes use throwing implements appropriate for their age group. The competition takes place on 30 May 2026 at the Koeru sports track. Participants can score points across several events, and winners are awarded cups and medals.

name: Maardu kevadjooks
description: The Maardu Spring Run and Health Walk is a traditional sports day held in Maardu, bringing together people of all ages who enjoy being active. The event features several runs and health walks for different age groups and abilities, including children’s races, a youth run, a walk for people with special needs, and 3 km and 5 km runs. Participation is free, and every finisher receives a medal. The event aims to offer the joy of movement, a sense of well-being, and an active day in the fresh air, while celebrating time spent together with family and friends.
course_highlights: Several distances: 100 m children’s race, 1 km youth run, 500 m walk for people with special needs, and 3 km and 5 km runs
Health walk over a 3 km distance
Starts and activities take place on the main avenue beside the Maxima XX shopping centre
additional: Participation is free. Registration is open online until 29 May at 19:00, or at Maardu City Stadium from 14 to 29 May, 13:00–17:00. On the day of the Spring Run, on-site registration is available only for the 500 m walk for people with special needs. All finishers receive a medal. The day concludes with a lottery among participants. Registration and the award ceremony take place at the finish on race day. The event includes various running and walking distances and is intended for the whole family.

There are water stations along the course, and the event center also offers a children’s athletics workshop and pop-up shops.
