More information about registration, event sponsors, and raffle prizes is available on the website. Participants are responsible for their own health, and the event is open to all age groups.

name: XI Bieg Wśród Krasnych Pól
organizer: Gminne Centrum Czytelnictwa i Kultury w Krasnopolu
description: Bieg Wśród Krasnych Pól is a forest race held in the Krasnopol municipality, offering routes of approximately 10 km and 5 km, as well as a 5 km Nordic Walking event. The route runs entirely along forest gravel and grass roads, providing a connection with nature and pleasant running conditions. The race office is located at the Municipal Reading and Culture Centre in Krasnopol, and the start takes place in the afternoon. The event is open to all and organised for people who enjoy outdoor activities.
course_highlights: Routes of approximately 10 km and 5 km
Forest gravel and grass roads
Start and finish in the Krasnopol municipality
additional: The race office is open from 13:00 to 15:00 at the organiser’s headquarters at 1 Maja Street 1 in Krasnopol. Parking is available in permitted places in the town, as marked on the map. The running and Nordic Walking routes are free of charge; the organiser asks participants to register responsibly. Race packs are distributed from 11:00 to 13:30. The event includes a 5 km Nordic Walking category, starting at 15:00 from the stadium at the Primary School in Krasnopol. Participation is free, and participants can support charitable causes.

name: ÜLEMISTE Ööjooks - Tallinn 2026
description: ÜLEMISTE Night Run - Tallinn 2026 is a running and walking event taking place in the Ülemiste district of Tallinn. The event offers an opportunity to get active and support well-being and health. It is part of a wider initiative to promote recreational physical activity in Estonia, organised by the Centre of Competence for Recreational Physical Activity. Participants can enjoy being active in an urban environment and support their mental and physical health.
course_highlights: Running and walking in the Ülemiste district of Tallinn
A great opportunity to get active and support your health
Organised by the Centre of Competence for Recreational Physical Activity
additional: Participation involves running and walking; registration is open

name: Lääne-Virumaa jooksusari 2026 - 20. Tapa linnajooks
description: The Lääne-Virumaa Running Series is a traditional running and walking series offering a variety of opportunities for different age groups and ability levels. Its events take place in different locations across Lääne-Virumaa, giving runners the chance to experience both urban and trail running. The 20th Tapa City Run takes place on 8 August 2026 at Tapa Gymnasium and is part of the series’ long-standing tradition of bringing together recreational athletes and running enthusiasts. The series aims to motivate people to stay active and provide enjoyable running experiences.
course_highlights: A varied route in an urban setting
Suitable for different age groups and ability levels
Part of a long-running series in Lääne-Virumaa
additional: The series offers different distances and age groups, including youth and children’s races. Events take place in different locations across Lääne-Virumaa, with both urban and trail runs. Registration is usually via online forms, but no direct registration link for the 20th Tapa City Run was found. The series contacts are Vahur Leemets and Ainar Sepnik. The event takes place at Tapa Gymnasium and offers online registration. Participants can choose from different distances, and awards are presented at every event.

name: Paldiski liigub
description: Paldiski Moves is the third stage of the Western Harju Movement Series and takes place at Paldiski Sports Centre. The course passes Paldiski’s main attractions, streets and pedestrian and cycling paths, offering participants beautiful natural views and a historic atmosphere. Free children’s races are held for younger family members, emphasising the joy of movement and lifelong awareness of physical activity. The event takes place as part of Paldiski City Day, where the series’ top finishers are awarded prizes, and the evening ends with a concert.
course_highlights: The course passes Paldiski’s main attractions
Runs along streets and pedestrian and cycling paths
Beautiful natural views and a historic atmosphere
additional: Chip timing is used, except for the untimed distance. The children’s races are free and intended for children aged 0–12. There are no placements; every finisher receives a diploma. The event is held in cooperation with Paldiski City Day, which offers activities for the whole family, and the series’ top three finishers are awarded prizes on the main stage. The evening ends with a concert. The children’s races are free, the course passes attractions, and chip timing is used (except for the untimed distance).

name: Stora Stöten Run
description: Stora Stöten Run is a trail race in the heart of the Falun Mine World Heritage Site, offering a historic and varied running experience. The course passes medieval smelting sites, mining farmsteads, dams and dam houses, following old routes known as Vattnets Väg till Gruvan (The Water’s Way to the Mine). The race has three distances (21.6 km, 13.6 km and 5.6 km) and welcomes both competitive runners and recreational participants, with the option to run timed or untimed. The event is organised by the orienteering club OK Kåre, which welcomes participants to the start and finish at Falun Mine.
course_highlights: Three courses: 21.6 km, 13.6 km and 5.6 km, starting and finishing at Falun Mine
The course passes medieval smelting sites, mining farmsteads, dams and dam houses along Vattnets Väg
Varied terrain: gravel, grass, trail tracks, nature paths and short paved sections; an initial climb and clearly marked downhill sections
additional: Start and finish at Falun Mine; warm-up begins at 12:10 on Falu Rödfärg’s paved area (approximately 7 minutes), led by Friskis & Svettis; all courses start at the same time, and runners are divided into two optional groups based on target pace (group 1: women ≤6 min/km, men ≤5 min/km). Runners can choose to run with or without timing; prizes go to the first three finishers on each course, with raffle prizes for other participants; teams can be registered (teams of 3), and registrations can be transferred free of charge through the registration system. The race information mentions aid stations/water stops, parking, race office, showers/changing facilities and course markings. All three courses start and finish at Falun Mine; results from previous years are available.

name: Ölands Marathon
description: Öland Marathon is an open marathon starting and finishing in the square in Löttorp. The course is very flat and easy to run, entirely paved, and offers views of Blå Jungfrun. The race consists of an inner loop of 2.1 km and an outer loop of 11.2 km, repeated three times until the distance of 42.195 km is reached. The race is organised by Högby IF and is aimed at recreational runners and masters categories in the stated divisions.
course_highlights: Very flat, easy-to-run marathon course
100% paved, officially measured by federation course measurer Carl‑Gustaf Nilsson
Start and finish in the square in Löttorp; a 2.1 km inner loop plus an 11.2 km outer loop repeated 3 times, with views of Blå Jungfrun
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 12:00. There are three aid stations per lap (approx. 13.3 km), serving sports drink (Umara), Coca-Cola and water; personal energy supplies must be handed in no later than one hour before the start. All finishers receive a medal/fossil made of Öland limestone; ÖM medals go to the top two in each category. The women’s and men’s winners receive dinner for two at Kalk in Löttorp. Accommodation is available in four-bed cabins at Högby IP. Aid stations: three per lap. The course consists of a 2.1 km section in Löttorp followed by an 11.2 km section: Löttorp - Alvedsjö - Kalmarsund - Gudesjö - Löttorp, repeated three times for a total of 42.195 km. Start and finish in the square in Löttorp; accommodation information is available via links on the organiser’s website.

name: Svartåloppet
description: Svartåloppet is a recurring running event held on the second Saturday in August, bringing together runners over several distances. The event offers 14 km and 5.5 km on hilly forest roads and trails, as well as a flat 2.5 km route on roads. The start and finish are at Svartå Folketshus, and timing is provided by Racetimer, delivering modern and reliable results. The event welcomes both recreational and competitive runners and highlights the local landscape and trail network.
course_highlights: 14 km and 5.5 km: hilly forest course on forest roads and trails
2.5 km: flatter route on roads
Start and finish at Svartå Folketshus
additional: Timing for Svartåloppet is provided by Racetimer, and results from previous years are published via Racetimer. The event is held annually on the second Saturday in August. The website contact is listed as Svartå Utvecklingsgrupp, telephone number 076 3073096. Three distances; children's race includes a medal and bag of sweets; on-site registration is available at the stated times (09:00–10:30), according to the event information.

name: Ångaloppet Trail
description: Ångaloppet is a welcoming swimrun event at Ånga gård, with the aim of making “swimrun for everyone.” The 2026 races take place on 8 August and include several distances and events for different levels, including 22 km, 11 km, Trail, 5 km and Family. The courses feature varied landscapes with forest trails, gravel roads and hilly, technical terrain; the swimrun races also include several swim sections in both lake and sea. The organisers emphasise a welcoming atmosphere for participants of all ages and experience levels.
course_highlights: Varied forest, trails and gravel roads
Hilly, technical terrain suited to trail running
Located between Lake Ången and the Baltic Sea—combining running and swimming (for the swimrun distances)
additional: In 2026, the event comprises five races on the same day (8 August): 22 km, 11 km, Trail, 5 km and Family. The 22 km race is a loop course (11 km per lap), with approximately 20 swim sections in total (the longest about 190 m and the shortest about 30 m), six aid stations along the course and a cutoff of 2.5 hours at the lap point. Team changes are possible for a fee of 400 SEK—email info@angaloppet.se. The courses are marked, and start group 1 (the earliest start) is listed at 10:00. Ångaloppet Trail is a new distance in the 2026 programme. Team changes are possible for a fee of 400 SEK. More information about equipment, safety, accommodation and parking is available on the event pages.

name: Häv och Gräv Vikbovändan 2026

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: vuxen 470 kr (fram till den 30/6, sedan kostar loppet 520 kr)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: duoklass: 940 kr per par (fram till den 30/6, sedan kostar duolopp 1040 kr)

description: Häv & Gräv Vikbovändan is a summer event on Vikbolandet in Östergötland where participants can choose to run or cycle. The main course is approximately 45 km long and runs mostly on paved roads and gravel (about 50/50), with several aid stations and samples from local farms along the way. There are categories for runners, cyclists, duos and children, and the event has a clear focus on local producers and an authentic farm setting. Pre-registered participants receive a collapsible cup (folding cup), which they must bring during the event to avoid disposable cups.
course_highlights: Main course approximately 45 km, about 50/50 gravel and asphalt
Aid stations at several local farms, with delicacies and opportunities to visit the farms
Opportunities to meet and sample products at farms with animals (ostriches, alpacas and yaks)
additional: The number of participants in the main event is limited (300). Online registration is open until 4 August; late registration is available from 09:00 in the start area until 30 minutes before each start (if places are available). Pre-registered participants receive a collapsible cup, which must be used during the event. The children's race (approximately 700 m or 1,400 m) requires no advance registration and is free for participants thanks to sponsorship from ICA (children receive a medal and ice cream). Toilets and showers are available at APPTEK's premises (open approximately 09:30–18:30). The running category is timed, with prizes for the top three women and men; the cycling and duo categories have special rules (helmets are compulsory, e-bikes are not allowed, and duo partners may swap as often as they like but must stay within 100 m of each other). There is a group warm-up before the start. Aid stations offer water and sports drinks; pre-registered participants receive a collapsible cup; everyone receives a medal; the event is not sanctioned by the Swedish Athletics Association; helmets are compulsory for cycling; the start and finish are in a floodlit trail setting; medical staff are on site; image rights rules apply. Register at vikbovandan.se/472-2/ or via the registration page on the main website.

name: Storå 6 timmars och 3 timmars
location: Guldsmedshyttan, Lindesberg Municipality, Örebro County, Sweden

name: Bėgimo varžybos „Jurbarkas 2026“, skirtos Nemuno metams paminėti
description: The “Jurbarkas 2026” running race, held to mark the Year of the Nemunas, will take place on August 8, 2026, in Jurbarkas, on Nemunas Street. Children, young people, and adults are all invited to participate, with three distances on offer: 400 m, 3 km, and 12 km. The event starts at 11:00. All participants who finish will receive commemorative gifts, and the best athletes will receive trophies. It’s a great opportunity to mark the Year of the Nemunas actively and run together in beautiful natural surroundings.
course_highlights: Three distances to choose from: 400 m, 3 km, and 12 km
The race takes place on Nemunas Street in Jurbarkas
The 12 km distance consists of 4 laps
additional: Race bib distribution starts at 10:00. Age groups by distance: 400 m — B12/M12 (born in 2014 or later); 3 km — B14/M14, B18/M18 (older participants compete without age-group ranking); 12 km — men and women in separate age groups. All participants who finish receive commemorative gifts, and the best receive trophies. Race distances: 400 m, 3 km, 12 km; age groups; advance registration; registration on the day of the event will not be available.

name: Šilutės naktinis bėgimas „ŠILUTĖ RUN 2026“
location: Šilutė, Šilutės rajonas, Klaipėdos apskritis, Lithuania
description: The Šilutė night run “ŠILUTĖ RUN 2026” is a nighttime running event for everyone who enjoys an active lifestyle—from families and beginners to experienced runners. The event takes place in Šilutė, with an illuminated night course, music, a great atmosphere and various activities. Participants can choose the 1 km run for families, children and pets, or the 5 km and 10 km distances. Participants will receive finisher medals, prizes will be awarded to the fastest runners, and tasty food will be available.
course_highlights: Illuminated night course
Location: Kiškio dauba, Šilutė
Distances: 1 km, 5 km and 10 km
additional: Event schedule: 18:00 bib collection, 19:30 official event opening, 20:00 1 km run for families, children and pets, 21:30 5 km and 10 km runs. Participants can enjoy music, prizes for the fastest runners, various activities and tasty food. Registration is open until August 7, 2026. The event program includes various distances and activities, and participants receive medals and prizes.

name: Druskininkų naktinis bėgimas 2026

price_tiers.distance: Bėgimo rungtys (1 km, 4 km, 8 km, 16 km, estafetė 2x4 km)

description: The Druskininkai Night Run is a unique summer night run in Druskininkai, inviting participants to experience the rhythm of running beneath the stars. The event features a vibrant atmosphere, music, light effects, and a scenic route around Lake Druskonis. Participants can choose from several events, including running, a relay, and roller skating, making it a great activity for families and friends. The run symbolizes friendship between Lithuania and Poland and is part of sports projects that promote cooperation between communities.
course_highlights: Scenic route around Lake Druskonis (1.2 km loop)
Night run with music, light and smoke effects
Option to participate in running and roller-skating events
additional: Race bibs and race packs are distributed at the event village from 20:00 to 21:40. Warm-up with a Zumba instructor. 21:25 – 1.2 km roller-skating event (untimed). 21:40 – 1,200 m run (untimed). 22:00 – 4 km and 12 km roller-skating events. 22:30 – starts for the 4 km, 8 km, and 16 km runs, and the 2×4 km relay. The event is part of the “Run Together with a Friend in Druskininkai” project, funded by the state budget. The event is funded by the Interreg Lithuania–Poland Programme. Participant bibs are issued on August 8; the start is in Druskininkai; several hundred participants are expected; this is an international project.

name: VI Ilgų nuotolių bėgiko Piotro Silkino jubiliejinis 85-mečio bėgimas
location: Kretingos Vasaros estrada, Maironio g. 15, Kretinga, Lithuania
description: The 85th-birthday run of long-distance runner Piotr Silkin is a traditional race held at Kretinga Summer Amphitheatre. The competition follows a lap format, with marathon participants completing one 2.2 km lap and twelve 3.3 km laps. The event celebrates longtime runner Piotr Silkin and attracts running enthusiasts from various places. Participants can enjoy both athletic competition and a welcoming community atmosphere.
course_highlights: The marathon course consists of 1 lap of 2.2 km and 12 laps of 3.3 km each
The competition takes place at Kretinga Summer Amphitheatre
The lap format lets spectators follow the race and support the participants
additional: Various distances and age groups will be offered at the event; results will be published, and registration is online.

name: Blodomloppet (Jönköping)
description: Welcome to Blodomloppet in Jönköping—a recreational event highlighting the need for blood donation, where you can walk, jog or run. In Jönköping, timed 5 km and 10 km races are offered, as well as an untimed 5 km walk. Children can take part in Lilla Blodomloppet (approx. 700 m), which has a mass start and a medal. Participants enter in teams, and the event traditionally ends with a picnic.
course_highlights: Distances: timed 5 km and 10 km races, plus an untimed 5 km walk
Lilla Blodomloppet: approximately 700 m for children up to 12 years old, with a mass start and medal; starts from Knektaparken
Event area at Knektaparken, with a traditional group picnic after the finish
additional: Team entries consist of 3–5 participants; registered blood donors receive a 40 kr discount if they indicate this when registering. Changes (e.g. from 10 km to 5 km) cost 50 kr; show your order ID when collecting your race pack. For registration on race day (11 August), payment is accepted only by Swish or cash. Other payment terms are 30 days, with several payment options (Swish, card via Swedbank Pay, postal giro, invoice). Team and individual entries have different prices; discounts are available for blood donors, and an invoice fee applies. Race numbers can be collected at Hovslätts IK’s clubhouse or at the start. The awards ceremony takes place at 19:30.

name: Kohila pikamaajooksude sari 2026 VI etapp 1000m
location: Kohila Spordikeskuse staadion, Kohila, Kohila vald, Estonia
description: Kohila Long-Distance Running Series 2026, Stage VI (1000 m), takes place at the Kohila Sports Centre stadium and is open to all running enthusiasts. The series features various distances and age groups, with participants earning points and winners determined by age group. The entry fee is €8, or €5 for young people and pensioners. Registration is primarily online in advance; on-site registration is available until 18:30. Series winners are awarded after the final race. To qualify for an award, participants must take part in at least four stages.
course_highlights: 400 m tartan running track at Kohila Stadium
Races over various distances, from 400 m to 5000 m
Age groups from young people to Veterans III (60+)
additional: Advance registration closes at 16:30 on race day. Late registrants are placed in the later heats, regardless of their expected time. On-site registration closes at 18:30. The top 10 in each race earn points; the total is calculated from each participant’s six best race results. Series winners are awarded after the final race. The entry fee is payable in cash on site. Advance registration is available at www.kohilaseeriajooksud.ee. Races take place at Kohila Stadium. Age categories and a points system are in place.

name: Filter Temposari (5. etapp)
description: Filter Temposari is Estonia’s oldest and most prestigious time-trial series, offering participants the chance to test themselves in cycling, running, or roller skating. The stages take place at various locations in Tallinn and the surrounding area, featuring individual time trials. The races are short and intense, suitable for both recreational and advanced athletes. The series also includes the Kullapada prize programme, which rewards consistent participation in every stage over the same distance.
course_highlights: Fast individual time-trial courses around Tallinn
Short 3–5 km runs and 7–17 km cycling courses
A new city sprint in the heart of Tallinn, featuring a 1.3 km course with a climb to Toompea
additional: Timing is accurate to a tenth of a second. Free warm-up trainers are available at the event centre. Hot Group: the final 10 minutes of each stage are reserved for the top cyclists. The courses are not closed to cars; competitors must obey traffic laws and keep to the right-hand side of the road. “I don’t have a time-trial bike” is no excuse—a standard road bike may be used. The event takes place at several different locations in Tallinn and includes time trials, sprint races, and special events such as the city sprint and series prizes.

name: 14. ETAPP / Järve terviserada
description: STAGE 14 / Järve health trail is a 10-stage relay race around Lake Viljandi, held on a health trail with varied terrain and different surface types. Teams consist of 10 members, with equal numbers of women and men, who take turns running the different stages. The start and finish are at Viljandi City Stadium, and organizers’ buses transport runners to the stages. The race is part of the tradition of the Great Run Around Lake Viljandi and offers a sporting experience for schools, companies, and sports clubs alike.
course_highlights: 10-stage relay race around Lake Viljandi on a health trail
Varied terrain and trails with different surfaces
Stages range in length from 500 m to 1,950 m
additional: Teams consist of 10 members (5 women and 5 men). Women run the odd-numbered stages and men run the even-numbered stages. Teams from institutions and companies may, as an exception, use a female runner on men’s stages. The entry fee is €50 for institutions, companies, and sports clubs; school teams pay no entry fee. Teams can register by email until 12 April, and runners must be registered by name at the stadium on 14 April. The awards ceremony takes place at 13:30 at the stadium. The three leading teams receive trophies and diplomas, and every participant receives a medal. Depending on trail conditions, the course may be changed to avoid muddy or snowy sections. A 10-stage relay race around Lake Viljandi, varied terrain, registration by email, start and finish at Viljandi City Stadium.

name: Jonavos bėgimo taurė - 2026, 4 etapas
description: The Jonava Running Cup is a traditional running series held in Jonava District to promote sport and physical activity. The competition is open to all runners, who can compete in different stages and age groups. Participants earn points at each stage toward the overall standings, while the courses run through various locations in Jonava District, offering an interesting and varied running experience. Registration is online, and race numbers are collected at the start venue on race day.
course_highlights: Stages take place in various locations in Jonava District: Šilai–Jaugeliškiai, Ragožiai, Juškonys, Salupiai–Bartoniai, Jonava
The start time for each stage is 19:30
Race numbers can be collected at the start venue on race day from 18:30 to 19:20
additional: Participants register separately for each stage. Participation is free. The courses may cross roads open to traffic, so participants must follow traffic rules. Registration deadlines vary by stage; race numbers are collected at the start venue on race day. Registration is online, the races take place in various locations in Jonava District, and participants are divided into age groups.

name: 31. Joosu Järvejooksu sarja 5. etapp
location: Viljandi Lake Health and Ski Trail, Viljandi, Estonia
description: The 5th stage of the Joosu Lake Run series is a running race organized by the Joosu sports club. It takes place on the health and ski trail around Lake Viljandi. The race gives participants the opportunity to enjoy beautiful lake views and varied terrain. It is a great opportunity for both recreational and experienced runners to take part in a friendly and supportive environment.
course_highlights: Health and ski trail around Lake Viljandi
Beautiful lake views along the route
Varied terrain suitable for runners

name: Vetlanda Citylopp

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Dam-, herr- och motionsklassen (10 km och 5 km) 180 kr

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Kids F8/P8 - F12/P12 (1 km till 1,7 km) 100 kr

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Föreningar (max 15st per anmälan) 900 kr (Föreningar kan anmäla i F/P8-F/P12 samt Junior 5km)

description: Vetlanda Citylopp is an open, spectator-friendly city race taking place on 14 August 2026, with the start and finish on Storgatan in Vetlanda. Runners can choose between 5 km and 10 km on a fast, looped course. There are also several children’s and youth classes, as well as a Funkis class. Bib collection and late registration are available at Stortorget from 12:00 on race day, and the event includes activities and simple food service in the square. Photos and videos will be taken during the race and may be used in future marketing.
course_highlights: Start and finish on Storgatan in central Vetlanda
Fast, spectator-friendly looped course (5 km or 10 km)
Children’s and youth distances from 400 m to 1.7 km, plus Funkis 1 km
additional: Bib collection and late registration are available at Stortorget from 12:00 on race day. Late registration is available until 30 minutes before each start time. Payment on site can be made via Swish (a surcharge applies for late registration). Timing is provided by Racetimer using a chip in the bib, and results are published live on Racetimer’s website and on the OK Njudung website. The event includes activities and simple food service in the square; the organizer will take photos and videos during the race. Participants can walk, jog or run at their own pace. On-site late registration is available for a fee. Photos and videos taken during the race may be used for marketing.

name: Lääne-Virumaa jooksusari 2026 - 27. Viru-Nigula Rahvajooks
location: Viru-Nigula jooksurada ja kaugushüppekast, Viru-Nigula, Lääne-Virumaa, Estonia
description: The Lääne-Virumaa Running Series 2026 offers a varied series of running and walking events, bringing together recreational athletes and enthusiasts from spring to autumn. The 27th Viru-Nigula Fun Run takes place on the Viru-Nigula running track and long-jump runway. It is part of a long-standing series that encourages participation across different age groups and distances. The series aims to promote healthy lifestyles and give participants the chance to test their abilities. The events are well organized, with chip timing, ensuring participants an enjoyable and motivating running experience.
course_highlights: A variety of distances, from 100 m to 10 km
Running courses on the Viru-Nigula running track and long-jump runway
A traditional event in the running series, with the running direction changing
additional: Timing is provided by a chip attached to the back of the bib and covered with foam board. Bibs must be fastened to the abdomen or chest, not the back. Competition categories are age-based, with scoring kept separately for each age category. Registration takes place on the running series website and closes at 16:00 on the day before the run. On-site registration is available at the times specified in the race guide. The competition offers various distances from 500 m to 27 km, with awards for the top three in every age category.

name: Midnattsloppet Stockholm
description: Midnattsloppet Stockholm is a festive evening race on Södermalm, taking place on 15 August 2026. It offers 21 km, 10 km and 5 km races, as well as several children’s and adaptive races. Late start times, music, spectators and activities along the course create a unique, lively atmosphere. The 21 km race covers two laps of the Midnattsloppet 10 km course, which is described as relatively hilly. The organisers highlight community, the joy of running, and the event’s appeal to both competitive runners and recreational participants.
course_highlights: 21 km = two laps of the Midnattsloppet 10 km course around Södermalm
A relatively hilly course, with climbs and the character of the neighbourhood
Music, samba rhythms and spectators along the course create a festival atmosphere
additional: Start area/warm-up: Ringvägen 26. Finish: Hornsgatan 57. The entry fee includes, among other things, a Björn Borg T-shirt (this year’s colour/design), chip timing, sports drink and water along the course, and a cold Vitamin Well, fruit and an energy bar at the finish. A medal can be purchased when registering, and a digital certificate is available. The organisers accept wellness benefits from Benifex, Epassi and Benefits, and provide instructions for using a voucher code; team registration gives a discount of SEK 50 per person. Information about start groups, T-shirts and race packs, as well as dedicated pages for companies, is available on the organisers’ website. The digital Midnattsloppet takes place from 12/9 to 20/9.

name: 6 sjöar
location: Fjällnora friluftsgård, Uppsala Municipality, Uppsala County, Sweden
description: 6 Lakes is a volunteer-run running event held on 15 August 2026, starting and finishing at Fjällnora Outdoor Recreation Centre outside Uppsala. Choose from a marathon (42 km around six lakes), a half marathon (21 km around four lakes), 10.3 km, or a shorter 5.5 km route around Lake Ramsen. All routes are well marked and feature a mix of forest trails and gravel roads. The event is environmentally conscious, with few disposable cups and the option of a reusable cup or Hydrapouch, and offers a free direct bus from Uppsala Travel Centre. It is a nature-focused race where a swim along the route may be possible in warm weather. Staggered start times let family and friends run different distances at the same time.
course_highlights: Marathon around six lakes; half marathon around four lakes, with scenic views of several bodies of water
Easy-running routes, mostly on small gravel roads and shorter trails, with a few technical sections (the 5 km route has tricky trails and bridges)
Opportunity for a swim along the route in warm weather, and aid stations along the courses
additional: Start and finish at Fjällnora Outdoor Recreation Centre. Start times: Marathon 10:00, Half Marathon 10:30, 10 km 11:00, 5 km 11:30. Race bibs can be collected at Uppsala Travel Centre on the Thursday or Friday before the event, from 11:00 to 19:00, or at the venue no later than 30 minutes before the start. Free direct buses from Uppsala Travel Centre use fossil-free fuel; the organiser will publish information and a timetable. The event avoids disposable cups: bring your own bottle or get a free reusable cup/Hydrapouch. Free T-shirts are not provided, but one can be purchased after the finish. The event is run by volunteers. For questions, contact info@6sjoar.se; a phone number for registration enquiries is listed on the contact page. Detailed maps and GPX files are available via the “Choose a race” page. Registration is online, and race bibs can be collected at Uppsala Travel Centre or before the start.

name: VIII-asis Žolinių maratonas
description: The VIII Žolinių Marathon is a traditional running event held in Vingis Park in Vilnius, celebrating the Žolinės holiday in a healthy, fun, and meaningful way. Both professional athletes and beginners can take part, with a range of distances from a children’s run to a full marathon. Each participant receives a metal statuette symbolizing a Žolinės plant. The course is a 5.275 km loop, which runners complete according to their chosen distance. The event promotes community spirit and an active lifestyle.
course_highlights: The course is certified by LAF measurer Alfonsas Kazlauskas
The loop is 5.275 km long; the marathon consists of 8 laps
The start is opposite the Vingis Park bandstand
additional: Participants can choose from 6 distances: marathon (42.2 km), 31.6 km, half marathon (21.1 km), 10.6 km, 5.3 km (one lap), and a 600 m children’s run. Each participant receives a metal statuette whose design changes each year, representing different Žolinės plants. The event celebrates tradition and community, offering a range of distances and symbolic awards featuring herbal plants.

name: XXI Bieg Lesoków
description: The 21st Lesoków Run is an annual race held in Szemud and part of the Kaszuby Biegają series. The event offers two courses, 5 km and 10 km, through the picturesque Kashubian countryside, encouraging people to spend time actively outdoors. It attracts runners of various age groups and ability levels, promoting a healthy lifestyle and local running culture.
course_highlights: The courses run through the charming Kashubian countryside
Two distances are available: 5 km and 10 km
The race takes place in the scenic surroundings of Szemud
additional: The event will take place on 16 August 2026, with online registration available from December 2025. The race is part of the regional Kaszuby Biegają series, which promotes physical activity in Kashubia.

name: 15. ETAPP / Vabaõhumuuseum
description: Tervisejooks and Walk is a multi-stage running and walking event held in various areas of Tallinn, including the Estonian Open Air Museum. Each stage offers a chance to enjoy beautiful nature trails and the pleasure of recreational sport. The Estonian Open Air Museum stage is 4.2 km long and is well suited to both runners and walkers who want to spend time actively outdoors. The event is a tradition and is open to everyone interested in recreational sport.
course_highlights: A 4.2 km route on the grounds of the Estonian Open Air Museum
A pleasant, peaceful natural setting
Suitable for both runners and walkers
additional: The stages take place on different weeks, and the registration period for each stage usually lasts one week. The event is held virtually, allowing participants to take part at a time that suits them during the registration period. The event is part of a recreational sports series that aims to promote healthy lifestyles and offer participants enjoyable, health-promoting experiences in a historic setting.

name: Convinistafetten
location: Stora Skuggan, Norra Djurgården, Stockholm, Sweden
description: Welcome to Convinistafetten in Stockholm—a festive, team-building relay at Stora Skuggan, Norra Djurgården. The event takes place over two late-summer evenings (19–20 August 2026). Each team has five people, and each participant runs 5 km. There is also a walking category for those who want to walk together. As an extra treat, title sponsor Convini provides every team with a picnic after the finish.
course_highlights: Five legs of 5 km—each team member runs 5 km
Start and finish area by the exchange zone at Stora Skuggan, Norra Djurgården
A picnic on the grass after the finish (provided for all teams by Convini)
additional: Teams register as a group of five. The walking team starts separately, and everyone in the team walks 5 km together. The team captain registers the team and receives information and all five race bibs by post; the runner on the final leg collects the picnic box from the picnic tent. A picnic is included in the entry (contents will be announced in May), and extra picnic boxes can be booked for SEK 495 each. Tent packages (Basic or Premium) are available as optional add-ons; orders are confirmed and tent locations communicated before the event. The minimum age for running 5 km is 13. A walking category is available; start times are assigned according to race number (for example, the first team starts at 17:30, followed by later teams at 17:33 and 17:36). Chip timing is included in the race bib. Changing rooms are available at Frescati Sports Center for SEK 40. RSIF offers a subsidised member price, with a deadline of 16 August at 18:00 to get a discount code. Information about parking and public transport is available.

name: IRONKIDS Tallinn 2026
location: Rocca Al Mare Kaubanduskeskus, Tallinn, Harju County, Estonia
description: IRONKIDS Tallinn 2026 is a children’s running competition held around Rocca al Mare Shopping Centre and Unibet Arena. The event is intended for different age groups and offers three distances: 350 m, 830 m and 1500 m. Starts are mass starts or rolling starts, with separate starts for boys and girls. Participants must wear the shirt provided by the organiser. The event is professionally organised, with timing on the longer distances and prizes and certificates for finishers.
course_highlights: The running routes follow roads around Rocca al Mare Shopping Centre and Unibet Arena
Mass start for the 400 m distance; rolling starts at intervals for the 830 m and 1500 m races
Separate classifications for boys and girls by age group
additional: On-site registration and kit collection take place at Rocca al Mare Shopping Centre on 19 August from 14.00 to 19.00 and on 20 August from 10.00 to 18.30. Participants must wear the shirt provided by the organiser and attach their race number to the front of their shirt. Start groups are marked with a coloured dot on the race number. The entry fee includes professional event organisation, timing for the 830 m and 1500 m distances, a finisher’s prize and an electronic certificate. The event is open to children born in 2019 or later. Registration closes on 18 August 2026, and the maximum number of participants is 1800.

name: 10. Üts Ummamuudu liina üüjuusk-kõnd
description: The 10th Üts Ummamuudu City Night Run-Walk is a physical activity event in the city of Võru, featuring running, Nordic walking and walking. The event is part of the activities of the Centre of Excellence for Physical Activity, which aims to promote an active lifestyle and good health. It welcomes everyone who wants to improve their wellbeing and enjoy exercise at different stages of life. The beautiful nature of Võru County provides a pleasant setting for physical activity.
course_highlights: Landscapes of the city and county of Võru
Suitable for running, Nordic walking and walking
Exercise for wellbeing and good health
additional: Võru city, Võru County; entry fees: free for children, €2 for others; registration via Stebby; chip timing and participation terms are provided

name: Sunset Run 2026
description: Sunset Run is a 5 km running and Nordic walking event held on the shared-use paths at Stroomi Beach and near Unibet Arena in Tallinn. The competition follows the competition regulations of the Estonian Athletics Association and is open to anyone who is sufficiently trained. Participants may complete the distance by running, walking or Nordic walking; walkers and Nordic walkers start at the back of the participant field. Separate age-group classifications are held for men and women. The event is organised by MTÜ Sportlik Eesti and MTÜ Triatloniakadeemia, which ensure professional organisation and participant comfort.
course_highlights: 5 km route on the shared-use paths at Stroomi Beach
Participants can run, walk or Nordic walk
The event takes place in the evening, with the start at 20:30
additional: Online registration is open until 23:59 on 18 August 2026. On-site registration and race-pack collection take place at Rocca al Mare Centre on 19 August from 14:00 to 19:00 and on race day, 20 August, from 10:00 to 17:00; they are also available by the Stroomi Beach Pavilion on 20 August from 18:30 to 20:15. Transfers to another participant are possible for an additional fee of €10 until 18 August 2026. The participation fee is paid via a bank link after completing the registration form. Age-group classifications apply, and participants take part at their own risk. The race offers running, walking and Nordic walking options; online and on-site registration; a 20:30 start; and a route on coastal paths and a promenade.

name: Hagbloms Nattloppet
description: Hagbloms Nattloppet in Kalmar is a 5.0 km night race offering an atmospheric running experience along Kalmar’s streets, with music, lighting and surprises along the course. The start and finish are at Stortorget, and the event is open to walkers, joggers and competitive runners. Everyone who finishes receives the Nattloppet medal, and those who register by 16 August also receive the race’s unique T-shirt. The event is organised by Högby IF (athletics).
course_highlights: Start, lap point and finish at Stortorget in Kalmar
5.0 km through the city along Kalmar’s streets, with music, lighting and surprises
A 5 km walking category without timing is available
additional: Race bibs and on-site registration are available at the Högby tent at Stortorget on Thursday 20 August from 15:00 to 17:00 and Friday 21 August from 18:00; on-site registration closes 1 hour before the start. All participants receive a medal, a drink, fruit and a piece of chocolate from ICA MAXI. Payment can be made by card, cash or Swish. Contact: Högby IF / friidrott@hogbyif.se, Jonne Svensson 070-693 87 44, Calle Nilsson 070-444 31 02. 5 km walking category without timing; race bibs and on-site registration at the Högby tent at Stortorget on 20 August from 15:00 to 17:00 and 21 August from 18:00; unique Nattloppet T-shirt for those who register by 16 August; drinks, fruit and chocolate for all participants.

name: XXXV-as tradicinis tarptautinis estafetinis bėgimas „Baltijos Kelias“
description: The 35th traditional international relay race “Baltic Way” will take place on August 21–24, 2027. The race symbolically retraces the 1989 Baltic Way, when millions of Lithuanians, Latvians, and Estonians joined hands in pursuit of freedom and independence. The approximately 650-kilometer route runs from Vilnius through Riga to Tallinn, with runners taking turns to cover stages of varying lengths. This is not only a sporting event, but also a living history lesson and a celebration of community, bringing together participants and supporters from the three Baltic countries.
course_highlights: An approximately 650 km route from Vilnius through Riga to Tallinn
A relay race through the three Baltic states
A symbolic reenactment of the historic human chain of the Baltic Way
additional: The race lasts four days, during which runners cover up to 200 kilometers each day. The event opens at Cathedral Square in Vilnius. Participants take turns in relay format, and the race is accompanied by meetings with people from towns and communities along the way. The event is part of the national physical activity program. It takes place over four days, with opportunities to meet and support the runners along the route, and commemorates the unity of the Baltic peoples.

name: Lüganuse rahvajooks
location: Kiviõli keskväljak, Kiviõli, Lüganuse vald, Ida-Viru maakond, Estonia
description: Lüganuse Public Run is part of the Ida-Viru running series and takes place at Kiviõli Central Square. The event offers several distances, from a children’s run to a 9 km run, and is suitable for different age groups and skill levels. Participants can enjoy a friendly, community atmosphere and compete in the friends’ group category. Registration is straightforward and the entry fee affordable, making this a great event for recreational and experienced runners alike.
course_highlights: Several distances: from the 300 m children’s run to the 9 km run
The race takes place at Kiviõli Central Square
Friends’ group category and a community-focused competition
additional: Participants can choose the Bronto children’s run (300 m), 2 km, 5 km or 9 km distances. The race office at the event centre is open from 10:30 to 11:55. Awards for all age groups will be presented together 15 minutes after the last competitor finishes. Competitors take part at their own risk. The entry fee can be paid on site in cash or via Stebby. The race takes place at Kiviõli Central Square. Registration is open both online and on site, and participants can choose from several distances.

name: Stockholm Trail
location: Hammarbyhöjdens IP, Stockholm Municipality, Stockholm County, Sweden
description: Dreaming of winding trails, sunlit rock slabs and delightful descents? Stockholm Trail offers several well-marked trail races in beautiful Nacka Nature Reserve, starting and finishing at Hammarbyhöjden IP, close to central Stockholm. The course suits both experienced trail runners and recreational runners looking to try trail running. Welcome to a challenging, sweaty and memorable trail event with encouraging race marshals and great service.
course_highlights: Technical forest trails and beautiful rock slabs with fantastic views in Nacka Nature Reserve
Start and finish at Hammarbyhöjden IP, about a 5-minute walk from Hammarbyhöjden metro station
Several aid stations (Umara sports drink) and a race bib with your name
additional: Start and finish at Hammarbyhöjden IP; race bibs can be collected on Friday 21/8 at Best Western Park City Hammarby Sjöstad, 16:00–19:00, or at the venue from 09:00 on race day. A wooden medal from Raw Cut Studio awaits finishers. Bag drop (supervised, free); indoor showers and changing facilities available. Name and distance changes are free until 8 August (contact sekretariat@stockholmtrail.se). Minimum age for the 21K is 18; time limits: 4 hours for the 21K and 3 hours for the 10K. Aid stations with water and Umara sports drink: the 21K passes 5 stations, the 10K 3 stations and the 5K 1 station. Premium packages with a T-shirt and training sessions are available; T-shirts can be purchased separately (349 SEK). Results are published online straight after the finish; there will be a speaker, music and refreshments at the venue. Distances include 21K, 10K, 5K, 5K Fun Run and 2.5K Minitrail; start/finish at Hammarbyhöjden IP; aid and energy stations along the course; bag drop and race-bib collection; the finish area offers drinks, coffee and refreshments, as well as indoor showers and changing facilities; this year, T-shirts will not be sold at the venue (buy them from Bagheera’s shop).

name: Hjorthagen Ultra Trail 100
description: Hjorthagen Ultra Trail 100 is an ultramarathon in Lill-Jansskogen in Stockholm, with a choice of 50 or 100 miles. The race celebrates endurance, nature experiences and community, and is run by Nisse and Anna Larsson through the Hjorthagen Ultra SC association. The start and finish are at Stora Skuggans väg 22, with ample parking and easy access to the metro and buses. Start times are 09:00 for 100 miles and 14:00 for 50 miles.
course_highlights: Magical forest sections in Lill-Jansskogen
Steep hills and plenty of elevation gain
Start/finish at Stora Skuggans väg 22, with good access to parking and public transport
additional: Cut-off times are 32 hours for 100 miles and 16 hours for 50 miles. Maximum 100 participants. Start times: 100 miles at 09:00 and 50 miles at 14:00. Surplus funds go to Suicide Zero.

name: Vilniaus bėgimo klubų taurė
location: Vingio parkas, Vilnius, Vilniaus rajonas, Vilnius, Lithuania
description: The Vilnius Running Clubs Cup is a running competition held at the Vingis Park Athletics Stadium in Vilnius. The event is intended for running clubs from Vilnius and other Lithuanian cities, sports clubs, families, children, young people, adults, seniors, and people with disabilities. The main event is a 5×1000 m team relay with five participants. Individual 1000 m races and a children’s 60 m race are also held. The event promotes physical activity, community spirit, and a healthy lifestyle in Vilnius.
course_highlights: The competition takes place at the Vingis Park Athletics Stadium
The main event is a 5×1000 m team relay
Individual 1000 m races and a children’s 60 m race are also held
additional: Competition schedule: 12:00 children’s 60 m race; 13:00 women’s 1000 m race and women’s tricycle race; 13:15 men’s 1000 m race and men’s tricycle race. The women’s, mixed, and men’s team relay events have been cancelled. The organizers reserve the right to adjust start times. The event includes various running events, including races for children, adults, and people with disabilities, and will take place on 28 August 2027.

name: Maraton Wigry
location: Stary Folwark, Wigierski Park Narodowy, Podlaskie Voivodeship, Poland
description: The Wigry Marathon is a unique marathon held within Wigry National Park, around the scenic Lake Wigry. The approximately 42.2 km course runs mainly along forest and unpaved paths, with a small proportion of asphalt, offering runners exceptionally clean air and beautiful views of the Suwałki and Sejny regions. This is not a marathon for setting personal bests, but for those who want to enjoy the exceptional natural surroundings and atmosphere. The event takes place on 22 August 2026, starting at the Monastery in Wigry and finishing at the Municipal Square in Stary Folwark.
course_highlights: The course is entirely within Wigry National Park
82% forest and unpaved roads and paths; 18% asphalt and sidewalks
Views of Lake Wigry and the clean air of the Green Lungs of Poland
additional: Transfer for participants to the start location. The technical briefing is optional. Bib transfers to another person are possible until the end of July 2026. A bonfire for participants and spectators after the race. The course map is available in GPX format. The event is scheduled for 22 August 2026, with online registration and a range of distances.

name: IV Maraton Wigry
location: Jezioro Wigry, Suwałki, Podlaskie Voivodeship, Poland
description: The IV Wigry Marathon is a unique marathon held in the scenic Wigry National Park, around Lake Wigry. The course runs mostly along forest and unpaved paths, with a short stretch of asphalt, offering runners pristine air and beautiful views of the Suwałki and Sejny regions. This is not a marathon for setting personal records, but for enjoying the exceptional nature and atmosphere. The start and finish are at historic locations, and after the race the organizers invite participants and spectators to a bonfire.
course_highlights: The course is entirely within Wigry National Park
82% forest roads, unpaved roads and paths; 18% asphalt and sidewalks
Views of Lake Wigry and the surrounding natural scenery
additional: The marathon starts at 09:30 at the Monastery in Wigry and finishes at 16:30 at the Municipal Square in Stary Folwark. The race office and registration are open until 08:30. The technical briefing is optional. Transfers to the start are available for participants. After the race, there will be an awards ceremony and a bonfire for participants and spectators. The course map is available in GPX format. The participant limit is 600 across both courses. Advance registration and an entry fee are required. The event also includes a shorter 13 km distance.

name: Blodomloppet Västerås
description: Welcome to Blodomloppet in Västerås at Rocklunda IP on 26 August 2026—a fun run for everyone, where you can walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km. Lilla Blodomloppet offers two children’s races (approx. 1,400 m and approx. 500 m), with a warm-up and the finish under the finish arch. The event is held to raise awareness of the need for blood donation and traditionally ends with a picnic for teams and participants. You can register individually or as part of a team (3–5 people); information and event details are available on the event website.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the Rocklunda area (the football pitches north of the riding arena)
The 5 km and 10 km courses are marked, with course marshals positioned along the routes
Lilla Blodomloppet: two children’s distances (~1,400 m, starting at 17:15, and ~500 m, starting at 17:25), finishing under the finish arch
additional: You can register individually or as part of a team (3–5 participants; the fee is always for 5 participants and includes a picnic for 5). Teams can be topped up to a maximum of 5 people until Monday 24/8, and the final date for team registration is stated as 19/8; larger companies can arrange a customer page/discount code. Children taking part in Lilla Blodomloppet receive a medal and a finish-line bag from ICA Maxi Hälla. The warm-up is in front of the stage at approximately 17:00, and children choose their distance on site. Registration is binding, cancellations are not accepted, and registration is open until 26/8 at 17:30. Course and map materials are available on the event website (link to map/course map). Register via the website or on site at Rocklunda IP from 15:00; 25 August according to the information page; includes a technical T-shirt, race bib and medal. Team registration is available for 3–5 participants, with the regular registration deadline on 20 August. The course route and start times will be announced by the organisers.

name: Norrköpings Stadslopp (Nkpg City)
description: NKPG City Norrköpings Stadslopp is organized by Tjalve Friidrott Norrköping and starts and finishes on Olai Kyrkogata in the heart of Norrköping. The event offers 5 km and 10 km distances (10 km is 2 x 5 km), as well as the free children’s race, Lilla Lundbergsloppet. The course passes through classic Norrköping settings, with large crowds lining the route, several music stations, and a mix of elite runners and recreational runners. Finishers receive medals and sponsored products. Team registration is available, and runners can choose timed or untimed participation.
course_highlights: A city course through classic Norrköping settings, with large crowds lining the route
More than ten music stations along the course to keep runners motivated
10 km = 2 x 5 km; start and finish on Olai Kyrkogata
additional: Start and finish on Olai Kyrkogata by Hötorget. Start times: Lilla Lundbergsloppet from 17:00 (four starts 15 minutes apart), 10 km at 18:30, 5 km at 19:30. Timed or untimed participation is available for the 5 km and 10 km. Lilla Lundbergsloppet (approx. 1,000 m) is free and limited to a maximum of 1,100 children; all children receive a medal and a goodie bag. Bib pickup: XXL Ingelsta on Tuesday 26 August, 11:00–18:00, and in the partner village at the start and finish area on Wednesday 27 August from 15:00 (late registration for the 5 km and 10 km is possible at both bib pickup locations). Start lists and information about your bib number will be published from the afternoon of Monday 25 August. Distance options: 5 km and 10 km; Lilla Lundbergsloppet is a free 1 km race for children; start and finish on Olai Kyrkogata; the course passes Linden shopping centre and features music stations along the way; Lilla Lundbergsloppet is limited to 1,100 children; all participants receive a medal and a goodie bag; the official results page is available online.

name: Naktinis bėgimas 2026
description: Night Run 2026 invites you to feel the rhythm of the night and immerse yourself in the end-of-summer buzz in Kaunas. It’s a unique opportunity to unwind from everyday life and end the summer with an energetic run featuring music, a sea of lights, and the company of enthusiastic runners. The event takes place in Town Hall Square and Santaka Park, offering spectacular views and an unforgettable nighttime adventure. Participants compete in the 2.5 km, 5 km, and 10 km distances, and the event is intended for both amateurs and professionals.
course_highlights: Course in Town Hall Square and Santaka Park
Night run with music and a sea of lights
Races over 2.5 km, 5 km, and 10 km
additional: Participants must attach their bib with the timing chip to the front of their shirt. Registration details and race distance can be changed until 2026-08-23 for a €5 fee. A participant’s time may not be recorded if they do not complete the course within the set time limit. The use of vehicles on the course is strictly prohibited. The event will take place in Kaunas; the course features a night run with lights, music, and a lively atmosphere. Registration and further information are available on the official website.

name: 22. Ülemiste metsajooks
description: The 22nd Ülemiste Forest Run is an environmentally friendly 3 km trail run held around the Tallinn Water Treatment Plant. The event centre, start and finish are located at Järvevana tee 3. The race takes place on Saturday, 29 August 2026, starting at 11:50. Participants are provided with a marked course, sports drink and water at the finish, and medical assistance along the entire route. The event is open to everyone interested in running and offers an enjoyable, athletic experience.
course_highlights: A 3 km forest trail around the Tallinn Water Treatment Plant
A marked course, with sports drink and water at the finish
Medical assistance along the entire route
additional: Race pack distribution and on-site registration begin at 9:30; payment can be made in cash. Timing is recorded using a chip attached to the back of the race number. Participants receive a medal, race number, timing, a result in the official results, services, sports drink and water at the finish. The event centre is on the grounds of the Tallinn Water Treatment Plant; parking and access are signposted. Children’s races for participants up to 12 years old are free and take place before the main race. The event includes a hiking trail, registration is on site, and family activities and warm-up exercises are also offered.

name: Sillamäe ultra 2026: Eesti meistrivõistlused 100 km jooksus
location: Sillamäe terviserada ja jõulinnakud, Sillamäe, Ida-Viru County, Estonia
price_range: 35.00 EUR kuni 31/07/2026, 50.00 EUR alates 01/08/2026 kuni võistluse päevani
description: Sillamäe Ultra 2026 is the Estonian 100 km running championships, held on the Sillamäe health trail and at the outdoor fitness areas on August 29, 2026. This is a traditional ultramarathon in which participants cover a road-running distance and compete for the Estonian championship title. The race offers a challenge to local and international ultrarunners who appreciate the variety of the course and the event’s organization. Sillamäe Ultra is known for its organization and strong participant community.
course_highlights: 100 km road race on the Sillamäe health trail and at the outdoor fitness areas
Estonian ultrarunning championships
Varied, well-organized course
additional: Participants can also enter the 50 km, 6-hour, and 12-hour races. There are facilities along the course for changing clothes and washing. Prizes are awarded to Estonia’s top runners, and the event is part of the Estonian ultrarunning championships.

name: Tallinna Vee 54. jooks ümber Ülemiste järve
location: Järvevana tee 3, Tallinn, Harju County, Estonia

price_tiers.distance: Tallinna Vee 54. jooks ümber Ülemiste järve

description: The 54th Tallinn Water Run Around Lake Ülemiste is a traditional running race taking place on 29 August 2026. The Run Around Lake Ülemiste is part of the Maru Lake Run Series, and this year’s race is the final, fourth event in the series. The marked course is 13.7 km long and starts and finishes at the Tallinn Water Treatment Plant, Järvevana tee 3. The race centre opens early in the morning, and race materials can be collected on site. Participants are provided with chip timing; the chip is attached to the back of the race bib.
course_highlights: A 13.7 km course around Lake Ülemiste
The course is marked and secured by course marshals
There are two water stations on the course
additional: Previous results are taken into account when forming start groups. All Nordic walkers must start in the last group. Participants receive a medal, and timing is provided by a chip attached to the back of the race bib. Children’s races for those up to 12 years old are free, with a distance of 250 m. Race materials can be collected at the race centre from 9:30 to 11:30. The race centre and start/finish are at the Tallinn Water Treatment Plant, Järvevana tee 3. The distance is 13.7 km, and the start and finish are at Järvevana tee 3. The event also includes a children’s race and a forest run, offering a varied experience for all participants.

name: Himos Trail
distance_verbose: 50 km, 36 km, 26 km, 18 km, 10 km, 7 km, 1 km

name: Jönköping Marathon & Half Marathon
description: Jönköping Marathon & Half Marathon is a welcoming city race taking place on 29 August 2026, with beautiful views along Lake Vättern and through Jönköping and Huskvarna. The course has been redesigned to reduce the total elevation gain while retaining a varied profile with sections through nature, crowd support and several power zones; the marathon course finishes with a spectacular finish line right in the middle of Munksjö Bridge. The race attracts international participants and also features shorter races and a MINI children’s race, as well as offers for businesses and tent packages in the start/finish area.
course_highlights: Spectacular finish line right in the middle of Munksjö Bridge
Beautiful views along Lake Vättern and through Jönköping and Huskvarna, on a redesigned course with less elevation gain
Marathon: 42,195 m with 12 aid stations along the course plus 1 in the start/finish area, an interactive map and power zones
additional: Practical information from the website: up to five runners can be registered at a time; race bibs are not sent out. The marathon course has an interactive map and a downloadable PDF, power zones, and 12+1 aid stations. The organizer offers tent packages for businesses in the start/finish area and the option to use a wellness allowance. Distances: 21K (21,097.5 m) and 42K (42,195 m); includes a team relay and MINI Jönköping Marathon for children. Energy and aid stations along the course, chip timing, group registration for up to 5 runners, and a business village with tents in the start/finish area.

name: Stockholm Halvmarathon
location: Kungliga slottet, Stockholm, Stockholm County, Sweden
description: The adidas Stockholm Half Marathon is a 21,098-metre half marathon that in 2026 will make its 25th run through central Stockholm. The course is unique, with both the start and finish in the area between the Royal Palace, the Parliament Building and the Opera House. It offers easy-to-run streets through Norrmalm, Vasastan, Kungsholmen, Gamla Stan and Södermalm. The first start is at 15:30. The event also includes an Expo and race-bib collection in Kungsträdgården from 27–29 August, as well as an after-run gathering in Kungsträdgården. The race is open to anyone turning 17 that year, and registration is binding.
course_highlights: Start and finish in the area by the Royal Palace/Norrbro, in the heart of the city
Easy-to-run course through Norrmalm, Vasastan, Kungsholmen, Gamla Stan and Södermalm
Passes, among other places, Hornsbergstrand, Rålambshovsparken and Söder Mälarstrand; detailed kilometre-by-kilometre course information is available on the course map
additional: Race-bib collection and Expo in Kungsträdgården from 27–29 August; after-run gathering in Kungsträdgården at the finish; registration is binding and the fee is non-refundable unless you have valid running-event insurance through Folksam; payment methods: online banking, Visa, MasterCard, Swish or invoice via Klarna; deadline for reporting results for seeding: 2 August 2026; late registration (subject to availability) from 24–29 August, up to 1 hour before the first start. 21.098 km course; start at 15:30; Expo in Kungsträdgården 27–29 August; start/finish by the Royal Palace; after-run gathering in Kungsträdgården.

name: Rynningeviken Längre 2026

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 24 augusti - 29 augusti (10.00/13.00) 625 SEK. Begränsat antal platser.

description: Rynningeviken Longer is a timed race in the Rynningeviken Nature Reserve outside Örebro, where participants run as far as they can in either three or six hours. The course follows scenic trails along Lake Hjälmaren and the Svartån River. It is relatively technical but fast, and just a stone’s throw from the city centre. The race is open to all running styles and abilities—from walking to ultrarunning—and offers a community-focused day with support and aid stations. A separate KidsRun for the youngest participants is also part of the event.
course_highlights: 2,412.5-metre loop, mostly gravel paths
Two bridges account for the few metres of elevation; start/finish on cobblestones
Final 508-metre loop for the closing measurement, reducing wait time at the finish
additional: Start times and mandatory briefings: 6-hour race starts at 11:00 (briefing at 10:45); 3-hour race starts at 14:00 (briefing at 13:45); KidsRun starts at 11:30 (briefing at 11:15). Location: Gamla Oljehamnen, below Naturens hus; parking along Oljevägen. Timing uses a transponder borrowed at bib collection (a lost transponder incurs a charge of SEK 800); the final measurement is verified with a measuring wheel. There is no individual timekeeping—the result is the distance covered when time expires. Umara sports drink and water are provided, along with a well-stocked energy table (bars, fruit, crisps, pickled cucumber, Tosca cake and more). No changing rooms or showers are available. Public toilets are located at the start and about 1 km along the course. Registration is only through the partner AnmälMigNu (group and corporate registration via info@epictrail.se). Young people (born in 2008 or later) receive a 50% discount. KidsRun participants receive a medal, Festis and ice cream. The course loop is approximately 2,412.5 m, with two bridges and a final 508 m loop. Energy and fluids are provided (Umara). No changing rooms or showers are offered; toilets are near the start and about 1 km along the course. Registration window: 24–29 August. The 50% youth discount applies to those born in 2008 or later. Registration includes a place, bib, timing, a unique medal, sports drink and energy along the course. Register via AnmälMigNu; group/corporate registration via info@epictrail.se. Cancellation and insurance options are available; participation is at your own risk.

description: The Northern Lithuania Half Marathon 2026 will take place in Pakruojis District, in the northern part of Lithuania. The event aims to promote running culture and encourage residents to be active, offering scenic routes in popular tourist areas. The race will start and finish in Pakruojis City Park, where participants can enjoy not only the sport but also discover the nature and culture of northern Lithuania. The event brings together people of different ages and social groups to spend time actively and healthily.
course_highlights: Scenic routes in popular tourist areas
Start and finish in Pakruojis City Park
Discover northern Lithuania while running
additional: Bib collection is open from 8:00 to 10:00. The half marathon starts at 11:00, and the other distances start at 10:00. Registration will not be available on race day. Participants agree that photographs and video footage taken during the event may be used for marketing purposes. The event includes different distances and categories, and online registration is open until the end of August. The event date is September 4, 2027.

description: TEMPLE Kaunas Half Marathon '26 is Kaunas’s hottest summer running festival, taking place on August 29. The event offers four distances: a half marathon (21.089 km), 10 km, 5 km, and a 400 m children’s run. It is more than a race—it is a complete experience filled with excitement, adrenaline, and community spirit, welcoming both those aiming for personal bests and those who want to enjoy the atmosphere of a running festival. The event fills the city with participants’ smiles and invites you to become part of its story.
course_highlights: Four distances to choose from: 21.089 km, 10 km, 5 km, and a 400 m children’s run
A summer running festival in the city of Kaunas
An atmosphere filled with excitement, adrenaline, and community spirit
additional: The event takes place in Kaunas, Lithuania, on Saturday, August 29, with the start at 08:00. Distances include a half marathon, 10 km, 5 km, and a 400 m children’s run. The event is organized by TS Temple social club and TK Temple Kaunas Half Marathon. 4 distances: 21.089 km (half marathon), 10 km, 5 km, 400 m children’s run

description: The 16th Baltic Sea Coast Marathon is an annual running event held in the picturesque towns of Jastarnia and Władysławowo. Participants can choose between the marathon and half-marathon distances, both running along the seashore and offering exceptional views and atmosphere. The event attracts runners from various age groups, including the K60+ and M65+ categories. The participant limit is 250, ensuring an intimate and friendly atmosphere.
course_highlights: The course runs along the shore of the Baltic Sea
Picturesque views of the sea and the coastal towns of Jastarnia and Władysławowo
Available distances: marathon (42 km) and half marathon (21 km)
additional: The participant limit is 250. The K60+ and M65+ age categories have reduced entry fees. Registration is open from 16 March to 26 August 2026. The fee on event day is higher. The start and finish are in the coastal towns of Jastarnia and Władysławowo. The participant limit is 250; registration opens on 16 March 2026 and includes information about dates and fees.

name: 9. Kristiine Rahvajooks
description: The 9th Kristiine Community Run takes place on 30 August 2026 at the playground in Löwenruh Park, Tallinn. This is a family event featuring children’s races for children up to 10 years old, in addition to the main 5 km distance. The event centre, start and finish are located beside Löwenruh Park, providing a pleasant and safe setting for running enthusiasts. The event aims to promote running as an accessible form of exercise and offer a sporting experience for different age groups.
course_highlights: 5 km course (2 × 2.5 km) on the streets of Kristiine and in Löwenruh Park
Children’s races for children up to 10 years old, 300 m without timing
Event centre, start and finish beside the playground in Löwenruh Park
additional: Registration for the children’s races takes place on race day from 10:00. The event centre opens at 10:00, and race-pack distribution begins at the same time. The award ceremony is scheduled for approximately 12:45 or after the last participant finishes. A competition category will be held even if there is only one participant. Finishers receive medals; the winner is awarded a trophy, and the top three receive prizes. The event takes place on 30 August 2026 and also includes children’s races and various activities, which start at 10:00 and end at 12:45.

name: Vikingatrailen
location: Årsunda IP, Årsunda, Sandviken Municipality, Gävleborg County, Sweden
description: Årsunda IF invites you to Vikingatrailen on Sunday, 30 August 2026—a trail race starting at Årsunda IP and finishing at Vikingabyn (Årsjö gård). The courses are 21 km, 10 km, 5 km and a 1 km mini race. Information, the invitation and course materials are published on the event website. Participant information, race instructions and start lists will be updated on the website before the race, and results and photos from previous years are also available. GPX files and maps (as well as elevation profiles via Garmin Connect) are available for all courses.
course_highlights: Start at Årsunda IP; finish at Vikingabyn (Årsjö gård).
Several distances: 21 km, 10 km, 5 km and a 1 km mini race (the mini race starts 1 km from the finish, with bus transport to the start).
Maps, GPX files and elevation profiles are published; the courses are available as public routes on Garmin Connect.
additional: Race instructions (version 2) updated with information including a football match at IP, bib numbers for the 1 km race, the awards ceremony and results. Registered participants and provisional start lists are published on an ongoing basis, starting around one month before the event. GPX files, maps and elevation profiles are available to download; the courses are also available as public routes on Garmin Connect. GPX files and maps are available; elevation profiles are planned; start lists, results and photos are updated on an ongoing basis; bus transport to the start is available for the 1 km race.

name: Alytaus Pusmaratonis – 2026
description: Alytus Half Marathon 2026 invites all running enthusiasts to a special summer finish in Alytus. The event starts and finishes in Alytus Town Hall Square, and the course passes through the city’s most beautiful spots—lush green parks, charming streets, and the banks of the Nemunas. Participants will experience a sense of community, movement, and excitement, with a festive atmosphere and support awaiting them at the finish. It’s a great opportunity to discover Alytus and take home unforgettable memories, whether you’re aiming for your best result or simply spending a meaningful day.
course_highlights: The course passes through lush green parks
Charming city streets
Inspiring banks of the Nemunas
additional: Various race distances, registration required, medals for all participants, awards for top finishers

name: 17. ETAPP / Paljassaare poolsaar
description: STAGE 17 / The Paljassaare Peninsula is part of the Stamina Health Run series and takes place on 2 September 2026 at the Paljassaare Beach car park in Tallinn. The race distance is 6.5 km, and the route winds through the scenic terrain of the Paljassaare Peninsula, offering participants an enjoyable challenge and a chance to enjoy nature. The event is suitable for both recreational and experienced runners looking to take part in a recreational sports event. The organiser, Stamina, ensures a smooth and enjoyable race experience.
course_highlights: A 6.5 km route on the Paljassaare Peninsula
Scenic nature and coastal terrain
Suitable for both recreational and experienced runners
additional: Contact person: Urmo Raiend, phone +3725019572. The list of registered participants is updated once every 24 hours. The venue is the Paljassaare Beach car park. Several stages take place at different locations in Tallinn, and registration and further information may be available on websites.

description: Join in celebrating the life-saving act of blood donation at Blodomloppet Växjö on 2 September 2026. The event offers 5 km and 10 km (10 km = two laps of a course-measured 5 km route), as well as Lilla Blodomloppet for the youngest participants. The start and finish are in Linnéparken, and the course is described as flat and fast, with plenty of crowd support along the way. The event welcomes both individual participants and teams, and traditionally wraps up with a picnic and activities in the event area.
course_highlights: Start and finish in beautiful Linnéparken, in front of the main stage
Flat, fast, course-measured 5 km route (10 km = two laps)
Separate walking route for the 5 km walk and a dedicated loop for Lilla Blodomloppet (~600 m)
additional: You can register individually or as part of a team (maximum 5 participants per team). Team members can take part in different distances. The deadline for team registration is 26 August 2026. An Excel template is available for bulk registrations, and the organiser can help set up a customer page or discount code for companies registering more than 20 participants. Changing a name or changing category/distance costs 50 SEK. Registration is open until the day of the event, and you can also register on site in Linnéparken (at the late-registration and race-number pickup tent). Lilla Blodomloppet takes place on its own loop in Linnéparken, with the same start and finish. Course details: the start and finish are in Linnéparken; the 5 km course is used for the 10 km race; on-site registration and team registration are available; a T-shirt, race number, medal and goodie bag are included; water stations and storage are mentioned.

name: Mägede järve jooks 8. etapp , Järvamaa Järvede jooksud sarjas
description: The Mägede Lake Run is the 8th stage of the Järvamaa Lakes Run Series and takes place in the Mägede sports area. This is a traditional local running event that gives participants the chance to enjoy beautiful nature and a sporting challenge. The courses run between lakes and forests, making them suitable for both recreational and experienced runners. The event is part of Järvamaa’s active sports calendar and welcomes all running enthusiasts.
course_highlights: The courses run between beautiful lakes and forests
Suitable for both recreational and experienced runners
Held in the Mägede sports area in Järvamaa
additional: Prizes are awarded to the top participants in the men’s and women’s categories, and participants can enjoy the beautiful scenery of the lake loop.

description: The Lääne-Virumaa running series is a traditional running and walking series offering distances suited to different age groups and ability levels. Its stages take place in various locations across Lääne-Virumaa, giving runners a variety of interesting routes. The series offers both the excitement of competition and the chance to enjoy good company and nature. Aseri Clay Run is one of the series’ events and takes place at the Aseri Leisure Centre.
course_highlights: Varied routes across the Lääne-Virumaa region
Different distances for children and adults
Stages in a long-running race series
additional: The series offers a range of distances, from children’s runs to the main races. Participants include both young and older running enthusiasts. The stages take place at different locations across Lääne-Virumaa, and the running direction may change from year to year. Participants can choose from different distances, and registration takes place online. Results and information are published on the series website.
