description: Uppsala Running Club welcomes elite runners, recreational runners and children of all ages to the King Bear Race, Uppsala’s cross-country race with families at its heart. The race takes place at OK Linné’s clubhouse and offers several distances (10 km, 6 km, a trail race and children’s races). The event now has set start times, race-number collection with electronic chips and an awards ceremony, as well as the race’s 20th anniversary in 2026.
course_highlights: The course is mostly gravel roads and forest trails, with some sections of asphalt
Three distances: approx. 10 km, just over 6 km and a trail race of approx. 5 km; the courses are marked every kilometre
Water stations: two on the 10 km course and one on the 6 km course; water is also available at the finish
additional: Race numbers with electronic chips can be collected at Löplabbet, Dragarbrunns Torg 6, on Friday 19 September from 12:00 to 18:30, or on race day from 09:00 until one hour before each start (30 minutes before the children’s races). Those who collect their race number on Friday get 20% off regular prices at the Löplabbet store (excluding electronics). Paid parking is available; the organisers recommend public transport (bus route 7) or cycling. Changing rooms and showers are available, but space is limited. There is a kiosk on site, an awards ceremony at approx. 13:30 and a prize draw. Start groups: the 10 km has start group 1 (under 50 minutes) and group 2; the 6 km starts in one combined group. Members who have completed at least one volunteer shift can register for free via kb.loppet@gmail.com. Water stations; race-number collection at Löplabbet (Dragarbrunns Torg 6); Swish payment; start times: 11:00 (10 km), 12:00 (6 km), 12:15 (trail); awards ceremony at approx. 13:30; a medal for all finishers; paid parking; public transport or cycling recommended; no timing for the children’s races.

name: Kistaloppet
description: Kistaloppet is a family-friendly urban running event organised by Löparakademin, with races for all ages: Kistaloppet 5 km, Lilla Kistaloppet/Fun Run 1.6 km and Kistaloppet MINI for the youngest participants. The courses offer a varied running experience through the million-programme high-rise housing area, the green spaces of Järvafältet and Kista’s IT cluster, with the start and finish at Jan Stenbecks torg next to Kista Galleria. The event emphasises accessibility and community (including the #RUN4ZERO initiative) and is designed both for recreational runners and for those who want to race on the officially measured 5 km course. The event is usually complemented by music, entertainment and a festive atmosphere along the course.
course_highlights: Officially measured 5 km course through Kista, passing high-rise buildings, the green spaces of Järvafältet and the IT cluster
Start and finish in a central location on Färögatan at Jan Stenbecks torg, next to Kista Galleria
Music stations/DJs and entertainment along the course create a festive atmosphere
additional: Registration is free and includes a medal; registration is open through 17 September (subject to availability). Race bib collection is at the event centre in Kista Galleria (premises opposite McDonald’s): Friday 19 September 12:00 - 18:00 and Saturday 20 September 09:15 - 13:00 (race bibs must be collected at least 30 minutes before the start). There is a water station at the finish; medical staff will be on site. Only the adult race (Kistaloppet 5K) has general timing; the other races, including Fun Run, are untimed. Volunteers are expected to be available from approximately 09:00 - 15:30. Races for the whole family: 5K, LILLA Kistaloppet, Kistaloppet MINI and Fun Run; registration is free; Lilla Kistaloppet is approximately 1.6 km and MINI is 500 m; all who complete Lilla Kistaloppet receive a medal; start times and race bib collection are at Kista Galleria.

name: Black River Run, 100 miles
location: Västerås SOKs klubbstuga Orientalen, Västerås, Sweden
description: Black River Run is an urban ultramarathon in Västerås, offered over several distances: 100 miles (161 km), 50 miles (80.5 km), Instegsultra (48 km), 20 miles (32.2 km) and 10 miles. The start, lap point and finish are at Västerås SOK’s clubhouse, Orientalen, which has changing rooms, showers and a sauna. The course consists of a varied 10-mile (16.1 km) loop featuring technical trails, running tracks, gravel roads, hiking trails and some asphalt. The race is organised by Västerås Löparklubb. Finishers receive a medal, and runners who complete the 100 miles in under 24 hours receive a belt buckle.
course_highlights: One loop is 10 miles (16.1 km); the race consists of repeated loops
Varied surfaces: technical trails, running tracks, gravel roads, hiking trails and some asphalt
An urban course, with the start, lap point and finish at Västerås SOK’s clubhouse, Orientalen
additional: Distances: 100 miles, 50 miles, Instegsultra (48 km), 20 miles and 10 miles. The start, lap point and finish are at Västerås SOK’s clubhouse, Orientalen, which has changing rooms, showers and a sauna. 100-mile runners who complete the course in under 24 hours receive the BRR belt buckle; other finishers receive a medal. Participants may decline the medal, in which case the organiser donates SEK 20 to Médecins Sans Frontières. The course is permanently marked with red posts. The 100-mile distance has a 24-hour time limit.

name: Lietuvos aklųjų ir silpnaregių lengvosios atletikos bėgimo plentu čempionatas
location: Zelvė, Elektrėnų savivaldybė, Vilniaus apskritis, Lithuania
description: The Lithuanian Blind and Visually Impaired Athletics Road Running Championship is a specialized running event for blind and visually impaired athletes. The competition takes place in Zelvė, Elektrėnai Municipality, and is organized by the Lithuanian Blind Sports Federation (LASF). Since 1990, the federation has actively supported sports for blind and visually impaired people in Lithuania, aiming to provide equal opportunities to take part in various sports competitions and events. The championship is an important tradition that encourages physical activity and a sense of community among athletes.
course_highlights: The race takes place on roads in Zelvė, Elektrėnai Municipality
For blind and visually impaired athletes
Organized by the Lithuanian Blind Sports Federation
additional: The event promotes inclusion and the development of sport among athletes with visual impairments. It will take place on September 19, 2026, in Zelvė.

name: Bėgimas „Ateik ir įveik!", skirtas prof. K. Baršausko atminimui
description: The “Come and Conquer!” run is a traditional event organized by Kaunas University of Technology in memory of Prof. K. Baršauskas. Participants are invited to test themselves on a variety of running and walking routes, including a new 5 km run with dogs. It is a great opportunity to spend time actively, promote a healthy lifestyle, and take part in a community sports event. The race takes place at the KTU Stadium and in Ąžuolynas Park. Participants receive commemorative medals, with prizes awarded by age group.
course_highlights: The race starts and finishes at KTU Stadium (Radvilėnų pl. 19, Kaunas)
Events: 10 km run, 5 km run, 5 km run with dogs, 5 km walk, 200 m children’s obstacle race
Part of the entry fee is donated to an animal shelter
additional: Event schedule: race bib collection from 10:30 to 11:50; 10 km run starts at 12:00; 5 km run, run with dogs, and walk start at 12:10; 200 m children’s race starts at 13:40; awards ceremony at 13:55. Registration is free for members of KTU sports teams. The entry fee is transferred to the Lithuanian Association of Amateur Runners’ account. Transfer of a participant’s race bib is prohibited. Awards are given to the KTU faculty/administrative unit team with the highest participation, as well as to the youngest and oldest participants. Routes: running and walking; age groups: children under 12, adults; online registration until September 18; the entry fee is transferred to the Lithuanian Association of Amateur Runners.

name: Run in Sopot IV - Opera Leśna
organizer: Miejski Ośrodek Sportu i Rekreacji w Sopocie

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: 5 km - mieszkańcy Sopotu posiadający Kartę Sopocką

description: Run in Sopot Opera Leśna is a 5 km race taking place on September 19, 2026, in Sopot. The start and finish are located in the parking lot by the Forest Opera, and the course runs through the picturesque surroundings. The race is part of a series of four events held on different dates and at different locations in Sopot, offering participants a unique atmosphere and the chance to compete over a short distance. The participant limit is 250, ensuring an intimate and well-organized event.
course_highlights: A 5 km course around the Forest Opera in Sopot
Start and finish in the parking lot by the Forest Opera
The race takes place in picturesque parkland and green spaces
additional: The participant limit is 250. Only runners wearing race bibs and people performing organizational duties may be on the course. Runners line up at the start in the designated area. The finish is at the same location as the start. The event includes several editions, with the main race taking place on September 19, 2026; discounts are available to Sopot residents with a Karta Sopocka card; the courses include beach and park areas; participants receive medals and drinks.

name: Rakvere 43. Rahvajooks
description: The 43rd Rakvere People’s Run is a traditional sporting event that welcomes everyone interested in running. The competition takes place at Rakvere City Stadium and offers a range of distances for both children and adults. The courses have been carefully selected to provide an enjoyable running experience and support a healthy lifestyle. The event is open to anyone sufficiently trained to complete their chosen distance.
course_highlights: 13.6 km running course
Nordic walking poles are not permitted on the course
Separate distance for recreational walkers
additional: Race materials can be collected and on-site registration is available on 26 September from 14:30 to 19:30 and on race day, 27 September, from 12:00 to 13:30 at Paide Machinery Factory Sports Hall. Changes of distance or participant are possible until 23.09.2026. Participants are divided into age groups, and the competition is held according to the competition rules of the Estonian Athletics Association. The event also focuses on traffic management and parking options around Rakvere City Stadium, ensuring a convenient and safe experience for participants.

name: Kullervo-maraton 2026
location: Joutsenen urheilukeskus, Joutsenon, Lappeenranta, South Karelia, Finland
description: Kullervo Marathon 2026 will be held at Joutseno Sports Centre on Sunday, 20 September 2026. This traditional event offers Finland’s fastest marathon course, which is almost entirely paved and flat. The race includes a marathon, half marathon, 10 km and children’s minimarathon, making it suitable for runners of various levels. The course is well marked and has plenty of aid stations. Participants receive course support, a medal, coffee, a sweet bun and soup lunch at the race restaurant.
course_highlights: The course is almost entirely paved and practically flat, with the exception of a small climb on a connecting section
Distances are marked every 3 km with colour-coded kilometre signs
There are two aid stations along the course, approximately every 4 km; the half marathon also has one additional aid station on the first lap
additional: The race office is located at Joutseno Hall and is open on Sat 19 Sep from 17:00 to 19:00 and Sun 20 Sep from 8:30 to 17:00. Race numbers must be collected from the race office. The maximum time limit is 6 hours for the marathon; there is no time limit for the half marathon or 10 km. Changing rooms, showers and toilets are available at Joutseno Hall. Free supervised baggage storage is next to the race office. Late registration is available at the race office on Sat 19 Sep from 17:00 to 19:00 and from 8:30 on Sun 20 Sep, closing one hour before each distance starts. Payments at the race office are accepted by card or MobilePay only. Participation can be deferred to the following year with a certificate from a healthcare provider, or transferred to another person by 17 September 2026 at the latest. Registration is online, and entry fees include course support, a medal, coffee, a sweet bun and soup lunch. The marathon is for participants over 18, and no advance registration is required for the children’s minimarathon. Late registration is also available on race day, and participation can be deferred to another year with a certificate from a healthcare provider.

name: KOMIA Kyrkösjärven kierros
description: KOMIA Kyrkösjärven kierros is Seinäjoki’s legendary and popular running event, held around Kyrkösjärvi. The event venue is Kyrkösjärvi Beach and the Käpälikkö Nature Centre, where the start, finish, parking and event centre are located. The main distance is a 15.4 km route. There is also the shorter, approximately 4.3 km Pikku Kyrkkäri for young participants or as a jog, and the 400–500 m Mini Kyrkkäri for the youngest family members. The event offers a memorable running experience surrounded by nature and is open to participants across different age and competition categories.
course_highlights: 15.4 km route around Kyrkösjärvi
One water station approximately halfway along the route, offering water and sports drink
The start, finish and event centre are all at Kyrkösjärvi Beach
additional: Bib collection and registration at the event office from 9.30 to 10.45. Runners start together in a mass start. Mini Kyrkkäri starts at 11.10. Baggage storage and gear transport are available in the finish area. A café is located in the event centre. Changing facilities and toilets are in the beach changing rooms. Participants receive a commemorative prize. Littering in nature is prohibited. Participation is at your own risk; leisure-time insurance is recommended. First aid is available in the finish area and at the water stations. The event includes several distances and age groups, and registration is available online or on site. The course follows nature trails, and the event is held annually in September at Kyrkösjärvi.

name: Hökensås Trail
description: Hökensås Trail is a trail race taking place on 20 September 2026 in the area around First Camp Hökensås, outside Tidaholm. The race offers three distances: 19 km, 11.5 km and 5.5 km, with the start and finish at First Camp Hökensås between 10:00 and 14:00. Organizer CKU6 (Cykelklubben U6) offers the race as part of Motionsloppet, in collaboration with Grebbestad Multisport, according to the information provided. The terrain combines forest roads and trails with roots and rocks, offering nature-close challenges in the Hökensås area.
course_highlights: Distances: 19 km, 11.5 km and 5.5 km
Start and finish at First Camp Hökensås in Tidaholm
Start times between 10:00 and 14:00
additional: Distances: 19 km, 11.5 km and 5.5 km; starts from First Camp Hökensås; Start times 10:00–14:00; Sports drink supplier: Umara; Organizer: CKU6 as part of Motionsloppet; Contact: hokensastrail@motionsloppet.se

name: Coop Linköping Runt
price_range: Gratis för LGIF-medlemmar; övriga deltagare pris ej angivet
description: COOP Linköping Runt is a city race in Linköping, starting and finishing in Trädgårdsföreningen. The race is organised by Linköpings GIF (LGIF) in collaboration with COOP Linköping, and registration is through cooplinkopingrunt.se. For LGIF members, the race is free with the campaign code LGIF2024; the price for other participants is listed on the website. The event is also looking for volunteers and offers a clear city-run experience in central Linköping.
course_highlights: Start and finish in Trädgårdsföreningen, in central Linköping
A city run focused on central Linköping
The LGIF2024 campaign code makes the race free for LGIF members
additional: The website includes sections on Time & place, Registration fee, Registration, Timing, Prizes, Time limit, Race bibs, Race confirmation, Transfer of entry, Category change, Unable to attend/Insurance, Changing & showers, Bag drop, Toilets, Warm-up, Food & drink, Energy, Medical care, Results and Terms. Registration through cooplinkopingrunt.se; campaign code LGIF2024 makes the race free for LGIF members; volunteers are wanted.

name: Sicklaloppet
description: Sicklaloppet is an autumn running festival in Nacka that welcomes runners of all ages and abilities. The main event is a 10 km fun run along the beautiful lakeshores of Sickla and Hammarby Sjöstad, starting and finishing at Sickla Köpkvarter. There is also a 5 km Energilopp and Lilla Sicklaloppet for children up to 12 years old. The race offers a scenic, fast course, a wonderful atmosphere and plenty of crowd support. Sicklaloppet is organised by Järla IF Orientering and is a major community celebration for the whole family.
course_highlights: The course runs along the lakeshores of Sickla and Hammarby Sjöstad
The surface is approximately 60% asphalt, 30% gravel and 10% wooden boardwalk
Start and finish at Sickla Köpkvarter, with beautiful scenery and crowd support
additional: Race bibs can be collected from partner XLL Sickla köpkvarter in the days before the race and on race day. The event venue opens at 08:00 and offers services and food trucks. There is a warm-up on site before the start. Race-day registration is available for an increased fee if the event is not sold out. Everyone who finishes receives a medal. The 10 km starting pen opens at 12:30. The 10 km time limit is approximately 1 hour and 15 minutes; after that, a rope will be put across the course at Kyrkviken for safety reasons. Terrain: scenic course along lakeshores, registration via partner XLL Sickla köpkvarter, family-friendly event, includes children’s races

name: Bėgimas „Molėtai bėga-2026“
organizer: Molėtų sporto centras, Lietuvos bėgimo mėgėjų asociacija
description: Molėtai Sports Center, together with the Lithuanian Amateur Runners Association, invites everyone to the traditional “Molėtai bėga 2026” run, which will take place in Molėtai. The event offers a range of distances for participants of different ages and fitness levels, including 3 km and 400 m races for children, as well as age-group races for adults. The start is at Molėtai Stadium, and participants receive race numbers and timing devices. It is a great opportunity to spend time actively and join a community sports celebration.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Molėtai Stadium (Ąžuolų St. 10, Molėtai)
Participant age groups range from children to older adults
Different distances: 400 m, 3 km, and age-group races
additional: Race numbers and timing devices are issued from 10:00 to 11:00 at Molėtai Sports Arena. Registration will be canceled if the entry fee is not paid by 17:00 on 2025-10-03. Venue: Molėtai Stadium; registration: in advance and on race day; event type: community and sports event

name: XV Półmaraton Augustowski
location: Amfiteatr Miejski, Augustów, Podlaskie Voivodeship, Poland
description: The 15th Augustów Half Marathon will take place on September 20, 2026, in Augustów, starting at 1:00 p.m. by the City Amphitheatre. Participants will cover the half-marathon distance of 21.0975 km on a course equal to half the length of a marathon. The event is organized by the Augustów Swimming Association and is an important running event in the region.
course_highlights: Distance of 21.0975 km — a classic half marathon
Start and finish by the City Amphitheatre in Augustów
The course runs through the scenic areas of Augustów
additional: The event also includes other races and activities. Registration details and the start list are available on the website.

name: 12 Bieg Ziemi Puckiej
location: Połczyno, Puck County, Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland

name: 20. ETAPP
description: 20th STAGE is part of a running series organized by Stamina Sports Club, held on the Järve health trail in Tallinn. This stage gives participants the chance to enjoy a health trail close to the city, well suited to both recreational and experienced runners. The event is traditional and well organized, offering an enjoyable sporting experience and a sense of community. Participants can also enjoy beautiful nature and healthy exercise in the fresh air.
course_highlights: Järve health trail in Tallinn
A well-maintained health trail close to the city
Suitable for both recreational and experienced runners
additional: The competitions include disc golf, motocross, and running. Various activities are available for participants and spectators, and competition results and information can be found on the website.

name: Rava järve jooks, Liikumissari 8.Järvamaa Järvede jooksud 9.etapp
description: The Rava Lake Run is part of the Liikumissari 8th Järvamaa Lakes Runs series and takes place by Lake Rava in Järvamaa. Runners of different age groups take part, from young children to older participants. A special feature of the race is completing one lap around the lake, with the fastest men and women receiving awards. This is a traditional, community-focused running event that offers both a sporting challenge and the chance to enjoy nature.
course_highlights: Complete one lap around the lake
Suitable for a range of age groups, from young children to older participants
Takes place by Lake Rava, amid beautiful natural surroundings
additional: The Järvamaa Lakes Runs series standings are kept across several age groups: young children (born in 2020 or later), 2016–2019, 2013–2015, 2010–2012, 1992–2009, 1972–1991, and 1971 or earlier. The fastest men and women to complete one lap around the lake are awarded. The event is open to different age groups, and the course is suitable for both runners and walkers. Raffle prizes are also awarded during the season, with prizes presented to the top participants at the end of the year.

name: Petzl Nuuksio Night Trail
description: Petzl Nuuksio Night Trail is an autumn night trail-running event held in the dark on forest trails in Nuuksio National Park. The event starts from Luukki Outdoor Recreation Centre in Espoo on 25.9.2026 and offers a route of approximately 13 kilometres, challenging runners amid nature. There is a dedicated category for non-binary participants, and free gear storage is available. A headlamp is mandatory because the route runs through a dark forest.
course_highlights: Approximately 13 km of trail running on Nuuksio’s autumn forest trails
Run in a dark forest; a headlamp is mandatory
Event centre and start at Luukki Outdoor Recreation Centre, Luukintie 33
additional: The race office is near the start and finish, where runners can collect their race numbers and register on the day. The organiser does not rent headlamps, so participants must bring their own. Timing is handled by an electronic timing app, and race numbers must be clearly attached at chest height. The maximum time allowed is 2.5 hours. Free gear storage is available near the race office on event day. Cash is not accepted, including for on-the-day registration. 13 km trail run in forest, mandatory headlamp, race categories including a mixed gender series, registration and timing details, event facilities including changing rooms, showers, sauna, and parking.

name: TCS Lidingöloppet (Lidingöloppshelgen)
distance_verbose: 30 km, 15 km, 10 km, 5 km, 5 km, 1.7 km

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 200 kr till och med 6/9 2026 (Gruppanmälan öppen tom 6/9)

description: TCS Lidingöloppet is the world’s largest cross-country race and takes place on the last weekend of September on Lidingö. The weekend offers events for all levels—from a 1.7 km children’s race to the classic 30 km race—and attracts over 30,000 runners to its scenic, hilly courses. The event is both a competitive challenge and a celebration of running, with a Sports Expo where you collect your race number and meet exhibitors. The natural surroundings and soft trails are hallmarks of the race.
course_highlights: Hilly, soft trails through forest and open areas, alternating between flat meadows, gravel roads, sloping paths and steep hills
TCS Lidingöloppet 30 km: approximately 522 metres of elevation gain
TCS Lidingöloppet 15 km: approximately 250 metres of elevation gain; starts at Koltorp and finishes at Grönsta Gärde
additional: Everyone who finishes receives the TCS Lidingöloppet bronze medal, featuring a unique Carl Milles design each year. A silver medal is available if you meet the silver-medal time and started in starting group 2 or lower. A diploma is provided as a PDF in the results email (a printed diploma can be ordered for 50 kr, including postage). Enervit offers on-course support stations (product stations for a fee). Minimum ages: 30 km = 17 years, 15 km = 15 years (other races have various age limits). The Sports Expo is used for race-number collection and features exhibitors. Lidingöloppet is a non-profit, association-run organisation (contact: Vasavägen 82, 181 41 Lidingö; telephone 08-7652615; email info@lidingoloppet.se). The early Early Bird discount (20%) has already been deducted from prices marked with *. Plan your experience: race-number collection, partners and exhibitors are on site. Environmentally friendly travel options include a free bus from Ropsten to Lidingövallen, runner buses from several locations in central Sweden, bicycle parking and carpooling. Access is limited and parking is scarce during the event. Seeding race ahead of the weekend: Vårmilen can be purchased as a seeding race (price 100–200 kr).

name: Greičio ratai 2026
location: Vilnius Vingio parko stadionas, Vilnius, Lithuania
description: Speed Laps 2026 is a running competition taking place at Vingis Park Stadium in Vilnius on September 25, 2026. The event includes 60 m races for children, 1,000 m races with special categories for people with disabilities using tricycles, and 5×1,000 m relay races for mixed, men’s, and women’s teams. The competition aims to promote running as a healthy lifestyle, popularize athletics, and determine the strongest teams. Participants must follow the rules, and the event is open to everyone; registration takes place in advance.
course_highlights: Vingis Park Stadium in Vilnius
60 m races for children’s age groups
1,000 m races for people with disabilities using tricycles, and 5×1,000 m relay races
additional: The men’s and women’s tricycle races are free of charge. A relay team consists of 5 runners, and no runner may run more than one leg. Participants must wear their bib on the front of their shirt. The use of vehicles and having a personal escort are prohibited during the competition. Walking animals on the course is prohibited during the event. Musical performances, a laser show, and other activities promoting an active lifestyle will take place during the event.

name: #BeActive bėgimas, skirtas Europos sporto savaitei
description: The European Week of Sport #BeActive event in Vilkaviškis is an important community tradition, inviting people of all ages and fitness levels to spend time being active. The programme includes relays, active games, football, wrestling and chess competitions, line dancing, exercise, Nordic walking and a group walk around the town. The evening programme culminates in a group dance and an energetic “Dance party” with Zumba rhythms, bringing participants together and highlighting the importance of movement in the community.
course_highlights: Relays and active games for children
Football, wrestling and chess competitions
A group #BeActive walk through the streets of Vilkaviškis
additional: Participants can join a variety of activities, from relays to chess, followed by a group dance and a “Dance party.” The event is for all age groups and fitness levels, highlighting community spirit and the importance of movement. The Vilkaviškis event is a major part of European Week of Sport #BeActive, engaging the local community in a range of sporting activities.

name: ELKE Tallinn Run - Noblessner 2026
description: The ELKE Tallinn Run takes place in Noblessner, offering the joy of exercise and experiences for the whole family. This beautiful seaside area provides an ideal setting for both sporting activities and an enjoyable day out. Race day begins with a children’s run and offers a choice of distances to suit both beginners and experienced runners. In addition to sports, the programme includes a free concert and a varied programme, creating a wonderful atmosphere for all participants and spectators.
course_highlights: The beautiful seaside area of Noblessner
Views of Noblessner and North Tallinn
A variety of distances for children and adults
additional: Race day begins with the children’s run at 13:00. The 2.5 km and Stebby 5 km distances start at 14:30, and the Neptunas 10 km distance starts at 15:10. The event centre’s programme runs from 11:00 - 17:10. A free concert by INGER takes place at Noblessner Central Square at 13:40. Outdoor seaside setting, family-friendly, includes a run and a concert, autumn event

name: 44. Viking Window Paide-Türi rahvajooks
description: Viking Window Paide-Türi Folk Run is a traditional mass-sport event that brings together running enthusiasts from Järvamaa and beyond. The course features varied terrain, offering both challenges and beautiful views. The event is suitable for all age groups and, alongside the main race, also offers children’s races and other active activities. Completing the course between Paide and Türi is an annual major event that brings the community and sports enthusiasts together.
course_highlights: Running route between Paide and Türi
Varied terrain and beautiful views
Suitable for all age groups
additional: Alongside the main race, the weekend also features children’s races and the Paide Heart Jog. Bus schedules between Paide and Türi and changes to traffic arrangements have also been organized as part of the event. Competition centre maps and live results are available online. Children’s races and fun runs suitable for the whole family and community also take place on race days.

name: 24. Jooks ümber Võhma
location: Võhma Kooli staadion, Võhma, Lääne-Virumaa, Estonia
description: The 24th Run Around Võhma is a traditional 5 km running event held on the streets of Võhma and along its health trail. The course is mostly hard-surfaced, with arrows marking the route on the asphalt, and a cyclist rides ahead of the competitors. The event is open to everyone born in 2020 or earlier and is suitable for both runners and walkers, including Nordic walkers, who start from the last row. Electronic timing is provided, and every finisher receives a medal. The event takes place at Võhma School stadium, which is also the start and finish venue.
course_highlights: 5 km course on the streets of Võhma and along its health trail
Mostly hard-surfaced, with arrows marking the route on the asphalt
A cyclist rides ahead of the competitors; the course is open to traffic
additional: Registration is available online until 24 September at timesport.ee, and on race day in front of Võhma School from 10:00 to 11:40. Timing is electronic, using a chip attached around the ankle, which must be returned at the finish. There is a €70 penalty for a chip that is not returned or is lost. Medals are distributed to participants, and prizes are raffled. Competitors are responsible for their own health. Children may take part at their parent’s responsibility. Registration is available both online and on site, and participants receive prizes and medals. The course runs along city streets and asphalt, offering a pleasant and motivating running experience. The event takes place on 26 September 2026.

name: 1. Full Moon Backyard Ultra Kymi
description: Backyard Ultra is an ultramarathon in which competitors run a 6.706-kilometre course within one hour. The race continues as long as multiple runners can complete a lap in under an hour, and the winner is the person who runs one lap more than the others. The course is either a loop or an out-and-back route, and the starting area remains the same throughout the race. There is no predetermined time limit, making the race particularly challenging and exciting. Backyard Ultra events are organised collaboratively in Finland, and the sport is actively being developed.
course_highlights: The course is a 6.706 km loop or out-and-back route
Each lap starts on the hour
The race continues as long as runners can complete a lap in under an hour
additional: A start warning is given 3, 2 and 1 minutes before the start. Competitors may not leave the course during a lap, except to use the toilet. Competitors must be in the starting area at the start, and the starting area remains the same throughout the race. Outside assistance and aids such as poles are not permitted. Slower runners must give way to faster runners. Timing lap times is optional. The event includes trail running on forest paths, and participants can use toilets, showers and shelter areas. The start is at Alakyläntie 67 in Kotka, and the course is approximately 6.7 km per lap.

name: Vihteljärven ympärijuoksu - 67.
description: The Vihteljärvi Circuit Run is Satakunta’s oldest continuously held annual running event, organized since 1960. The event offers a 6.5-kilometer race in several age groups, as well as a fun run without timing. There are also children’s events over shorter distances. The race takes place at Vihteljärvi School in Kankaanpää and offers participants a traditional, community-oriented running experience in a scenic setting.
course_highlights: 6.5 km race in several age groups
Children’s events over distances of 0.2–1 km
Satakunta’s oldest continuously held annual running event
additional: Registration and payment at the event venue from 10:00 onward; payment by cash, MobilePay, or ePass. Participants in the lake circuit can take part without timing from 10:00 onward. Children’s events start at 10:30 and the circuit run at 12:00. The top three in the competitive events receive prizes; every child participant receives a prize. A smart TV will be raffled among participants in the lake circuit. The event starts at Laviantie 1035 and also includes children’s events, with prizes for all participants.

name: Suojuoksun elämyskisa
description: The Swamp Run Experience Race is a unique running event held at Kauklaisten Ojassuo. The event gives runners the opportunity to challenge themselves and enjoy a different kind of running experience surrounded by nature. There are several route options of different lengths, suitable for both experienced runners and first-timers. Join us to enjoy the joy of running and a sense of community!
course_highlights: The run takes place in the scenic natural surroundings of Kauklaisten Ojassuo
Several route options: 1.4 km, 2.7 km, 4.1 km and 5.5 km
The event offers a unique running experience for both experienced runners and first-timers
additional: Registration takes place on site. The entry fee is €12 (€10 with a runner’s card) and includes raffle prizes and a medal. The race has categories for different route lengths, including M-General 5.5 km and T15 1.350 km. The event includes different types of running, such as road and trail running, but more detailed information about arrangements and participation is not available.

name: Lampaloppet 2026
description: Lampaloppet 2026 will take place on Saturday, September 26, 2026, at Lamminaho in Pyhäjärvi. The route winds through the scenery of Honkavuori and introduces runners to Ahto’s historic sites. The event offers a suitable challenge for both competitive runners and more casual participants. The competitive categories are timed, but there is also an untimed fun run where participants can move at their own pace. Participants can use the water stations, washing facilities and sauna, and receive a Lampaloppet neck gaiter.
course_highlights: The route winds through the scenery of Honkavuori
A chance to explore Ahto’s historic sites
Water stations at approximately 5 km and 10 km, and at the finish
additional: The entry fee includes a marked route, timing in the competitive categories, water stations, washing facilities and sauna, and a Lampaloppet neck gaiter. The top three finishers in the competitive categories will receive prizes, and an Ooni pizza oven will be raffled among all participants. The fun run is an untimed distance of the participant’s choice. The event also includes the Honkavuori Stair Community and a stair relay competition, which will be held in July 2026. Entry fees vary, and the event offers the opportunity to compete both individually and as a team.

name: XXVI Nidos pusės maratono bėgimas. Lietuvos pusės maratono bėgimo čempionatas.
description: The International Nida Half Marathon is a traditional annual event held in Nida on the Curonian Spit. The event includes a half-marathon distance, the 5 km YIT Run, and shorter distances for children and young people. It is a great opportunity for both professional and recreational runners to enjoy running in a unique natural environment and take part in the Lithuanian Half Marathon Championship. The event promotes physical activity and sport in Lithuania, and participants can expect professionally prepared courses and a friendly atmosphere.
course_highlights: 21.098 km half-marathon distance through the natural landscape of the Curonian Spit
5 km YIT Run course in an urban setting
Short races for children and young people, starting at Nida Port and in the town centre
additional: Starts take place at different locations: the half marathon starts by the Sakutis café (Naglių St. 14A), the 5 km YIT Run starts by the Catholic church (Taikos St. 17), and the children’s and young people’s races start at Nida Port and by the Neringa Municipality building. Race numbers are issued on event day from 8:00. Registration is not available on event day. The race courses are certified according to World Athletics and AIMS requirements. The awards ceremony will take place at 16:00 at Nida KTIC Agila. The event will be held on September 26, 2026, with a range of distances available, including children’s races.

name: VERTICAL VILNIUS 2026
location: Liepkalnio šlaitai, Vilnius, Vilniaus apskritis, Lithuania
organizer: TA Trail Akademija VŽ Vaidas Žlabys
description: Vertical Vilnius is Lithuania’s most vertical trail running race, held in Vilnius. Participants tackle the slopes of Liepkalnis, and the race offers the opportunity to earn ITRA ranking points. An eco-friendly “Trash Vertical” challenge is also organized to encourage participants to care for the environment. Registration is free, so everyone is invited to join in and test their abilities on this unique course.
course_highlights: Tackle the slopes of Liepkalnis
Trail running courses in Vilnius
Opportunity to earn ITRA ranking points
additional: Registration is free. Participants can take part in the eco-friendly “Trash Vertical” challenge. Trail, eco-friendly challenge, ITRA points, distances: 200 m, 600 m, 1000 m; the event takes place on the slopes of Liepkalnis in Vilnius.

name: 26-as Tarptautinis Nidos Pusės Maratono Bėgimas
location: Nidos kultūros centras, Nida, Klaipėda County, Lithuania
description: The 26th International Nida Half Marathon will take place on September 26, 2026, in Nida. The event offers a range of distances: a half marathon, the 5 km YIT Run, a 2 km youth run, and short children’s runs (500 m and 210 m). The race courses are certified in accordance with World Athletics and AIMS requirements, and the starts take place at different locations in Nida. This traditional event promotes physical activity and the popularity of running and athletics in Lithuania.
course_highlights: The 21.098 km half-marathon course is certified in accordance with World Athletics and AIMS requirements
The 5 km YIT Run course follows the streets of Nida
Short children’s runs (210 m and 500 m) take place at Nida Port and by the Neringa Municipality building
additional: The children’s runs start at 10:00 at Nida Port and by the Neringa Municipality building. Race bibs are distributed on event day from 8:00 until the start times. The awards ceremony is scheduled for 16:00 at Nida KTIC “Agila.” The event welcomes participants of various age groups, with starts at Nida Port and the cultural center; registration is online.

name: Vertical Vilnius
description: Vertical Vilnius is Lithuania’s most vertical trail running race, held on the slopes of Liepkalnis in Vilnius. Participants tackle steep hillsides to earn ITRA ranking points and take part in the ecological “Trash Vertical” challenge. The race promotes physical activity and care for nature, inviting runners to test their strength on a unique course.
course_highlights: Steep climbs on the slopes of Liepkalnis
Trail running course
Opportunity to earn ITRA ranking points
additional: Registration is free. The race includes the ecological “Trash Vertical” challenge. trail, vertical ascent, ecological challenge, free registration

name: Nocna Piątka 2026
location: Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk, Gdańsk, Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland
description: Nocna Piątka is a unique 5-kilometre race taking place on 26 September 2026 in Gdańsk, the day before the Garmin Gdańsk Half Marathon. The start and finish are on the illuminated track at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk, where participants can expect a spectacular show featuring lasers, music and light effects. The route winds through the city and is enlivened by spectator points with music and fire shows, creating a unique nighttime atmosphere. This new version of the well-known race accompanying the half marathon has moved to Saturday evening to offer runners and spectators a special experience.
course_highlights: Start and finish on the illuminated track at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk
City route with fire shows and spectator points featuring music and a DJ
Spectacular show featuring laser displays and energetic music
additional: The race takes place the day before the half marathon, with the start and finish at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk. It features a nighttime atmosphere with music, laser and fire shows, and spectator points with a DJ. An evening race with laser and pyrotechnic displays, starting at 20:00, on an illuminated route. An event accompanying the Garmin Gdańsk Half Marathon. The participant limit is not provided. Attractions and visual production are described as being of the highest standard.

name: Lääne-Virumaa jooksusari 2026 - 41. Jooks ümber Porkuni järve
description: The Lääne-Virumaa Running Series is a traditional running and walking series offering a variety of distances for different age groups and ability levels. Its events take place in beautiful locations across Lääne-Virumaa, giving runners both the excitement of competition and an enjoyable sporting experience. The main races, as well as youth and children’s races, are popular throughout the series and encourage physical activity and a healthy lifestyle. The series’ events have earned a firm place in runners’ calendars and hearts.
course_highlights: A variety of distances, from children’s races to the main races
Courses pass through scenic natural locations in Lääne-Virumaa
The series features a mix of running formats and traditional events
additional: The series includes separate races for children and young people. These are not official competitive distances, but they offer a valuable running experience. Events take place at different locations in Lääne-Virumaa, for example by Kadrina Reservoir, at the Simuna-Laekvere Run, and at the Kunda City Run. Participation has been high, with more than 200 athletes at the Kunda run, for example. The series also includes recreational walks and a range of age groups. Events feature different race distances and formats, including the main race, mini run, toddler run, children’s race, and youth race, and also offer the opportunity to take part in walking events.

name: Sportland Kõrvemaa Metsajooks 2026
description: Sportland Kõrvemaa Forest Run is a trail race taking place on 27 September 2026, offering participants the chance to run along beautiful trails through a pristine nature reserve. The race features distances of 21 km, 10 km and 5 km, as well as a youth run for participants up to 17 years old and free children’s runs. The routes run entirely through the nature reserve, offering breathtaking views and fresh air. The race centre is conveniently located near Tallinn, and the whole family can enjoy additional activities, childcare, a sauna and hot tubs. All finishers receive a medal and gifts; prizes are awarded to the winners, and the season’s best performers and teams are recognised.
course_highlights: The entire route runs through a stunning nature reserve
A trail run in pristine nature, with a mix of climbs and descents
Routes suitable for beginners and experienced runners alike
additional: The race centre opens at 10:00, children’s runs start at 10:40, and the group warm-up is at 11:45. After the run, free soup and a smoothie will be served, and the sauna and hot tubs will be open. A Sportland pop-up shop will be at the race centre. Prizes for the winners; the season’s best performers and teams will be recognised. Option to rent a private Iglusauna on the shore of the pond. Childcare and activities for the youngest family members. Finish closes at 15:30. Trail running, forest trails, family and children’s runs, registration and information HERE, a modern race experience and family events

name: 58. Vihtijärvihölkkä
price_range: 15 eur (enakko), 20 eur (paikan päällä) for half marathon; 10 eur (enakko), 15 eur (paikan päällä) for 10 km; 4 eur (enakko), 5 eur (paikan päällä) for 9-13 sarjat; 10 eur (enakko), 15 eur (paikan päällä) for other series
description: Vihtijärvihölkkä is a long-running running event offering competitors the chance to take part in a half marathon, a 10-kilometre run and shorter distances. The routes pass through varied terrain, with several water stations serving runners along the way. The event is open to different age groups and categories and is held in the Vihtijärvi area. The race has been held 58 times, reflecting its popularity and tradition among local residents.
course_highlights: Water stations on the half-marathon route approximately every 3–3.5 km
A water station at the 5 km mark on the 10 km route
Varied terrain and several distance and category options
additional: Race numbers must be collected at least 30 minutes before the start. On-site registration is possible up to one hour before the start of the relevant category. There are several water stations along the route, and payment can also be made using MobilePay code 27789. Participation is free for Vihtijärven Uhka members in the 9–17-year-old categories. Several distances, registration instructions, start schedules and route details are available; outdoor terrain in the Vihtijärvi area; free participation for children aged 9–17; an event medal can be purchased after the race.

name: TCS Lilla Lidingöloppet (Rosa Bandet-loppet)
description: The Pink Ribbon Race is part of TCS Lidingöloppet weekend on Lidingö and offers 4 km or 10 km of running in support of the Swedish Cancer Society. The race starts follow the Grönsta and Koltorp start times, and the courses are soft and scenic. From 2025, a new 4 km category for ages 9–15 (FP-9-15) is available. SEK 100 of the entry fee goes in full to the Swedish Cancer Society, and the Pink Ribbon Race@Home option is available for running at home. The Pink Ribbon Race is part of Lidingöloppet weekend and of Tjejklassikern and Kortklassikern.
course_highlights: 4 km and 10 km on soft courses through Lidingö’s scenic terrain
SEK 100 of the entry fee goes in full to the Swedish Cancer Society
New FP-9-15 category in the 4 km race from 2025 for younger runners
additional: The minimum age for Lilla Lidingöloppet is 7–15 years. Start times are listed by the Grönsta and Koltorp start groups, and warm-up and start corral rules are strictly followed. SEK 100 of the entry fee goes to the Swedish Cancer Society, and the Pink Ribbon Race is part of Lidingöloppet weekend, Tjejklassikern and Kortklassikern.

name: Garmin Półmaraton Gdańsk
location: Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk, Gdańsk, Pomorskie, Poland
organizer: Arena Gdańsk Operator Sp. z o.o.
description: Garmin Gdańsk Half Marathon is an annual running event held in Gdańsk, featuring a 21.0975 km course. The start and finish are located at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk. The race is open to mass participation, with starting corrals assigned according to declared finish time, and participants can also enter 4-person relay teams. The organizers provide professional timekeeping, medical support, refreshments and water along the course. The event promotes physical activity and a healthy lifestyle, and helps raise the profile of Gdańsk in Poland and abroad.
course_highlights: A 21.0975 km half-marathon course in Gdańsk
Start and finish at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk
Starting corrals assigned according to declared finish time
additional: The start and finish are located at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk. The start is divided into time-based corrals according to declared finish time (red, blue, green and yellow). Relay teams start from the blue corral. The race package includes a waterproof bib with a chip, timekeeping, medical support, water at refreshment points, refreshments after the finish and a medal. The full race package is guaranteed for payments made by 30.08.2026. The bib must be attached horizontally to the front of the shirt. Passing the bib to another person without the organizer’s consent is prohibited. The event includes various distances, including a half marathon and 5 km race, with a participant limit of up to 10,000. Registration takes place online, and fees can be paid via Przelewy24 or by traditional bank transfer. Races for children and teenagers are also available.

name: 13. Garmin Półmaraton Gdańsk Nocna Piątka
location: Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk, Gdańsk, Pomorskie, Poland
organizer: Akademicki Związek Sportowy COSA Oddział w Gdańsku
description: Garmin Gdańsk Half Marathon is an annual running celebration in the heart of the Tricity, taking place on September 26–27, 2026. The program will feature a new event, the Night Five: an evening 5 km run with light displays, fireworks, and cheers from spectators. The main event is the 13th edition of the half marathon, covering 21.0975 km and traditionally starting and finishing at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk. The course is fast and suited to setting personal bests, while the race has a unique atmosphere thanks to spectator support and beautiful urban scenery.
course_highlights: A fast 21.0975 km half-marathon course suited to setting personal bests
Start and finish at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk—the most beautiful stadium in Poland
Night Five: an evening 5 km run with light displays and fireworks
additional: Start and finish at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk. The Garmin Gdańsk Half Marathon start is divided into waves based on declared finishing time (red, blue, green, yellow). Relay teams start from the blue wave. The Night Five starts in the evening on 26.09.2026, after 20:00, with light displays and fireworks. Race packets will be distributed at Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk on 26–27.09.2026. The awards ceremony is scheduled for 13:30 on the day of the half marathon. The event also includes races for children over various distances, warm-ups, awards ceremonies, and registration opening earlier, on October 7. Participants can look forward to attractive cash prizes and record bonuses.

name: 16. ETAPP
description: The 16th stage is part of a recreational running series held in Tallinn. The event centre, start and finish are at Järve Health Trail, offering participants an enjoyable running and Nordic walking experience at the car park by the shared-use path. The route is easily accessible by car and public transport, making it convenient to take part. The series aims to offer everyone an opportunity to spend their free time in an active and healthy way.
course_highlights: Running and Nordic walking on Järve Health Trail
Start and finish at the car park by the Järve shared-use path
Easy access by car and public transport
additional: The event centre, start and finish are at the car park by the Järve shared-use path, at the Viljandi mnt end of Järve Health Trail. Those arriving by car are advised to park at Järve Selver, from where it is about a 400 m walk or jog to the event centre. Those travelling by bus should get off at the Risti stop, from where it is about a 300 m walk to the event centre.

name: Kauno rajono bėgimas 2026
description: Kaunas District Run 2026 is a traditional sporting event held at a distinctive location in Kaunas District: the square next to the Old Zapyškis Church of St. John the Baptist. The event promotes a healthy lifestyle and physical activity, bringing together running enthusiasts of all ages and abilities. Participants can choose from several distances, and the organizers provide a safe, technically prepared course and a pleasant atmosphere for everyone.
course_highlights: 5 km course along the cycling path from Zapyškis Church to the „Vandenis“ garden community and back
10 km course along the cycling path from Zapyškis Church to Kačerginė and back via Palankių, Prieplaukos, J. Janonio, Taikos, V. Mykolaičio-Putino and J. Zikaro streets and Liepų Park
Start and finish in the square next to the Old Zapyškis Church of St. John the Baptist
additional: On race day, the timing system will be switched off at 12:30, after which times will not be recorded. Participants must wear their bib with the timing chip attached to the front of their shirt. Start times by distance: 10 km – 11:00, 5 km – 11:05, 1 km – 12:45, children's 300 m races – 13:00. Parents, guardians or coaches are responsible for minors. Race regulations and registration are available via the links; the event invites participants to take part and enjoy the local surroundings.

name: Friday Night Run 2026
description: Friday Night Run is an energetic night run in central Tartu, taking place on 2 October at Town Hall Square. The distance is approximately 4 km, along city streets, offering a chance to enjoy the atmosphere of the autumn city with friends. This is not a race; participants can choose to run with or without timing. The event features music and a live concert, creating a lively evening atmosphere.
course_highlights: An approximately 4 km course in central Tartu
The course runs along city streets and park paths
One split-timing point on the timed distance
additional: The race number must be pinned to the chest and visible throughout the distance. The timing chip is attached to the back of the race number and is for single use. Participants have 45 minutes to complete the course; the finish closes at 21:45. The entry fee includes a marked course, race number, timing (if using a chip), services at the finish, and medical assistance if needed. Registration is available online until 2 October at 17:00 and on site until 20:30. The event includes online and on-site registration, medals and T-shirts for participants, and group discounts.

name: 15. Tartu Linnamaratoni Lastejooksud
description: The Tartu City Marathon children’s runs are open to all children, with the joy of taking part as the main goal. Recommended guidelines are provided for distances and age groups, but every child is welcome on the course and treated equally. Race numbers are handed out one hour before the start, and participants are not ranked. The event takes place at Tartu Town Hall Square, and children can register in advance or on site.
course_highlights: The children’s runs take place at Tartu Town Hall Square
All children are welcome, regardless of age or previous experience
All children receive the same race number (number 1), and the starting procedure is simple
additional: Those who register in advance will receive a unique QR code to collect their race number. Race-number distribution begins one hour before the start, near the Tartu Market Hall. All children start with race number 1. Participants can download and colour in a personalised diploma. Participants’ names will be published on the website after the event. Prizes will be drawn among all those who registered in advance. Several partners offer discounts to participants. Medals and diplomas are provided to all participants. Registration is available online and on site, and the entry fee is 4 euros.

name: Loimaan Lenkki
description: Loimaan Lenkki is an autumn running event held in the centre of Loimaa. There are four distances to choose from: 1.2 km, 2.4 km, 5.2 km and 10.4 km, making it suitable for a wide range of runners. The start is at Viljavarastontie 4, and the event offers a great opportunity to get active and enjoy a sense of community. Registration is open, and the event is organised by Loimaan Seudun Nuorkauppakamari.
course_highlights: Four distances: 1.2 km, 2.4 km, 5.2 km and 10.4 km
Start at Viljavarastontie 4, Loimaa
The event takes place in the centre of Loimaa
additional: Discounted prices are available for groups of at least 8 people and Junior Chamber members: €12 (10 km) / €6 (5 km). Start times for the shorter distances (1.2 km and 2.4 km) are at 12:30. The event also includes a family-friendly mini run and offers an opportunity to take part in community exercise. Participants can choose a race distance to suit their fitness and preferences.

name: KOMIA Esi-Talvijuoksusarja
description: The KOMIA Pre-Winter Running Series is a six-part winter running series that gives runners of all levels the opportunity to test their fitness and track their progress. The fast, flat routes start at Pajuluoma School and offer 2 km, 5 km and 10 km distances. The series begins with the Pre-Winter Run in early October and continues into spring. The top runners are rewarded at the end of the series, and the races are suitable for recreational and competitive runners alike.
course_highlights: Fast, flat 2 km, 5 km and 10 km routes starting at Pajuluoma School
Routes officially measured in October 2024
A six-part winter running series starting in October and continuing into spring
additional: The series offers a season pass that allows entry to all six events. There are also age categories for children (2 km), and the runner card gives a discount. The routes start at Pajuluoma School and are officially measured. The top runners are rewarded at the end of the series. A variety of trail and running events, registration information and series information.

name: Keurusselän Syyslenkki

description: Keurusselkä Autumn Run is a varied autumn event set in the beautiful surroundings of Keuruu, offering trail running and mountain biking. Trail runners can choose between two distances, 6.4 km and 12 km, while mountain bikers have several distances in different categories, including children’s and e-bike categories. The event also features children’s runs and the option to enjoy the hotel spa as part of the entry fee. The routes pass through the terrain around Resort Keurusselkä and Montosvuori, with hill running and technically varied trails. Participants can also enjoy special offers at the hotel restaurant on event day.
course_highlights: Trail runs of 6.4 km and 12 km through the terrain around Keurusselkä and Montosvuori
The mountain bike route includes technically easy outdoor trails and trail sections
Mountain biking features steep climbs and fast descents on Montosvuori
additional: Start and finish at Keurusselkä Resort. The entry fee includes use of the hotel spa. There is a water station along the route, and participants may set up their own aid stations. Payment when collecting the race number is by cash or MobilePay. The hotel restaurant has special offers on event day. Mountain biking has categories for different age groups and e-bikes. Children can sign up for their run on site. Trail running and MTB routes, a children’s run, and spa access included in the entry fee; the event takes place in the terrain around Keurusselkä and Montosvuori.

name: Hiit Out Trailrun 2027
location: Mellingerum, Oskarshamn Municipality, Kalmar County, Sweden

name: Ekerumsloppet
description: Welcome to Ekerumsloppet, an autumn cross-country race around Ekerum and Rällaskogen on Öland, organised by Högby IF Friidrott. The race offers 10 km for adults and approximately 1.3 km for young runners, starting at 11:00 and 10:00 respectively. The start and finish are at Ekerum Resort. The registration deadline is 26 September 2026; late registration is available at race-number collection from 09:00 on race day. The race follows cross-country trails through the forest around Ekerum and Rällaskogen.
course_highlights: Cross-country trails through the forest around Ekerum and Rällaskogen
Start and finish at Ekerum Resort
Two distances: 10 km for adults and approximately 1.3 km for young runners
additional: A cross-country race through the forest around Ekerum and Rällaskogen; Start and finish at Ekerum Resort; Registration deadline: 26 September 2026; Late registration at race-number collection from 09:00 on race day

name: John Bauer Trail Run
distance_verbose: 18 km, 10 km, 5 km, 5 km, 2 km, 0.4 km
price_range: 18 km: 400–700 kr; 10 km: 320–600 kr; 5 km upplevelseloppet: 160–300 kr; 5 km Stortrollens lopp: 120 kr; 2 km Knattetrollens lopp: 120–250 kr; 400 m: ej angivet
description: John Bauer Trail Run is a tough, hilly trail race held from the IKHP cabin on Huskvarnaberget. The race offers several distances (18 km, 10 km, 5 km, and several children’s/youth classes) and runs partly on trails and partly off-trail, with significant elevation gain and technical descents. A special feature is Strutsabacken, where climb times are recorded and the Bergatroll award goes to the fastest ascent. The event is family-friendly, with food and activities at the start/finish, as well as changing rooms and showers in the IKHP cabin.
course_highlights: Tough, hilly trail sections on both trails and off-trail terrain
Strutsabacken (the ski slope), with a separately timed climb and the Bergatroll award
Views over Lake Vättern and a technical descent through Ulvadalen
additional: Late registration is available on race day between 9:00 and 11:00. Race bibs with timing chips must be collected from the IKHP cabin by 11:15 and worn visibly at the front during the race; the chip does not need to be returned. Aid stations are located along the course (with kilometre markers for each distance). Changing rooms and showers are available in the IKHP cabin, valuables can be stored in a locked area at bib collection, and food is available at the start/finish. After finishing, participants are treated to a “troll menu” by the organiser (show your race bib). Hamburgers are served after the race; aid stations are available along the course; changing rooms and showers are available; Startklar insurance is available (175 kr/year); maximum 500 participants; race bibs must be collected from the IKHP cabin by 11:00.

name: Broloppet Motala
description: Broloppet Motala returns with a familiar yet new course, starting and finishing in Stadsparken in central Motala. The race is organised by Motala AIF Friidrott and offers short recreational distances suitable for a wide range of participants: both 5 km and 10 km are available. Promoted as one of Sweden’s most beautiful recreational races, the event welcomes recreational runners and runners of all levels to take part on 3 October.
course_highlights: Start and finish in Stadsparken in central Motala
A familiar yet new course through central parts of Motala
Short recreational distances (5 km and 10 km) suitable for recreational runners
additional: Organiser: Motala AIF Friidrott. The event is described as “Sweden’s most beautiful recreational race”. The website encourages visitors to save 3 October in their calendars and notes that prices apply until 28/9 (the next price increase). There are four distances: 10 km, 5 km, 1.5 km (youth) and 400 m (children’s race). Race numbers can be collected at Team Sportia on 2–3 October. The prize ceremony takes place in Stadsparken at approximately 14:30.

name: Förbifartspremiären
description: The Förbifartspremiären is a one-off event where you can run or walk on the new E4, both above ground and through its tunnels, before the road opens to traffic. The race takes place on 3 October 2026, starting and finishing at the new Akalla interchange, and is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. There will be a competitive class (approximately 12 km), a recreational class (choice of approximately 4, 7 or 12 km) and a walking class (Herr Gårman, approximately 4 km). The event is billed as a unique “once in a lifetime” experience—the chance to be among the first to set foot on the new road.
course_highlights: The route runs both above ground and through tunnels on the new E4.
Start and finish at the new Akalla interchange (Vandagatan).
The recreational class has exits after approximately 4, 7 or 12 km, so you choose your distance during the race.
additional: Registration opens on 5 February at 12:00. The race has a maximum time of 1 hour 30 minutes; the competitive class starts at approximately 09:00, the recreational class has start times between 10:00 and 17:30, and Herr Gårman (walking) between 18:00 and 19:30. Customer service: Gustavslundsvägen 18, 167 51 Bromma, telephone +46 8 545 66 440, opening hours Tuesday–Thursday 09:00–15:00 (lunch 12:00–13:00). Individuals can pay by card, Klarna invoice or Swish; company invoices are available only for groups of 20 or more through a designated contact. Registration is binding and personal. Registration opens on 5 February at 12:00; the first section, Hjulsta–Häggvik, is planned to open at the end of 2026; the entire Förbifart Stockholm is due for completion in 2030; starting places are sold through Marathongruppen; the race includes a race bib, timing, finish-line services and a medal; approximately 10,000 starting places were sold in the first hour.

name: VII-asis Utenos hipodromo maratonas
distance_verbose: Maratonas, Pusmaratonas, 10 km, 5 km, 3000 metrai, 1 km, 0.4 km
description: The 7th Utena Hippodrome Marathon will take place on October 3, 2026, in Utena, at a modern hippodrome in the Baltic states. The event offers 7 distances: marathon, half marathon, 10 km, 5 km, 3 km, a 1 km family run, and a 400 m children’s run. It’s a great opportunity for both experienced runners and families with children to spend time actively and test their abilities on a variety of courses.
course_highlights: The most modern hippodrome in the Baltic states
7 different distances, from a 400 m children’s run to a marathon
The event takes place at Utena Hippodrome, Užpalių St. 103
additional: Registration opens on 2026-04-01. Event organizers: MA Maratomanija and UB Utenos Bėgimai. For questions, contact maratomanija@gmail.com or call +37061532233. Registration opens on April 1, 2026. The event includes various distances and children’s races, and participants are expected from different locations.

description: Visahölkkä is a traditional running event held in the rural surroundings of Ojakkala on the first Sunday in October. The event has been organized since 2007, and participation has settled at 30–50 runners. Visahölkkä is part of the Vihti Hölkkäkunkku series and, in addition to competitive categories, offers a fitness category in which the fastest woman and man are awarded. The start is at Ojakkala School, and the event is open to runners of all ages.
course_highlights: A run through the rural surroundings of Ojakkala
The route is shown on the Visahölkkä route map
The event is part of the Vihti Hölkkäkunkku series
additional: Register by 12:45 at the venue or in advance by email. The top three finishers in the competitive categories receive awards. In the fitness category, the fastest woman and man receive awards. Payments should be made to Ojakkalan Visa’s account: FI11 4006 1520 0181 71. A route map is available. The run is part of the Vihti Hölkkäkunkku running series. Registration is available in advance or at the venue.

name: Solvalla Trail
location: Nuuksio National Park, Espoo, Uusimaa, Finland
description: Solvalla Trail returns to the trail-running calendar in the Nuuksio area of Espoo on Sunday, October 4, 2026. The event offers runners the chance to enjoy scenic trails over two distances: 9 km and 18 km. Organized by Esbo IF, it is suitable for both experienced trail runners and recreational runners. Join us for an exciting and memorable trail-running event in beautiful surroundings.
course_highlights: Trail running through the scenic terrain of Nuuksio
Two distances: 9 km and 18 km
The event takes place in Espoo on October 4, 2026
additional: Trail race in Nuuksio with 9 km and 18 km options, route marked in the forest, race day is October 4, 2026.
